literalEnglish: Under the deep blue sky, everyone searches for the moon.
Let me quickly gather my own beloved moon into my arms.
notes_20240423113656.childFriendlyEnglish: Everyone longs for someone dear to them. The speaker imagines finding that loved one like a moon in the wide blue sky and holding them close.
notes_20240423113656.simpleHindiExplanation: नीले आकाश में सब अपने-अपने चाँद को खोज रहे हैं। कवयित्री अपने प्रिय को चाँद मानकर उसे जल्दी से अपनी बाँहों में भर लेने की इच्छा व्यक्त करती हैं।
notes_20240423113656.context: The preserved record is dated 2022-10-15 and names “व्योम” (sky) as the मंच-provided word. The moon imagery appears personal and affectionate; no specific event is claimed.

literalEnglish: Through devotion to Shiva, Rohini protects her beloved's life.
Seated upon Shiva's head, Shashank—the moon—became exalted.
notes_20240423113758.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem connects devotion to Shiva with the moon's honoured place on Shiva's head, showing how faith can make someone feel protected and blessed.
notes_20240423113758.simpleHindiExplanation: इस दोहे में रोहिणी, चंद्रमा और शिव से जुड़ी पौराणिक छवियाँ हैं। भाव यह है कि शिव-भक्ति प्रिय की रक्षा करती है और शिव के मस्तक पर स्थान पाकर चंद्रमा गौरवशाली होता है।
notes_20240423113758.context: The prompt is “शशांक,” a name for the moon. The wording appears to combine Rohini's association with the moon and the familiar image of the crescent moon on Shiva's head; the exact intended story is uncertain.

literalEnglish: When hardship enters life, remember the Divine.
Those who pray with a compassionate heart find that their plea is heard.
notes_20240423113808.childFriendlyEnglish: When life feels difficult, remembering God and praying sincerely can give hope and the feeling that we are not alone.
notes_20240423113808.simpleHindiExplanation: कठिन समय में ईश्वर को याद करने और सच्चे, करुण भाव से प्रार्थना करने की सीख दी गई है। ऐसी प्रार्थना मन को भरोसा देती है कि पुकार सुनी जाएगी।
notes_20240423113808.context: The preserved prompt is “कष्ट.” The poem is devotional and offers spiritual reassurance rather than referring to a dated public event.

literalEnglish: Brahma, Vishnu, and Mahesh are the sustainers of the world.
Whoever worships them will never be overcome by distress.
notes_20240423113814.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem says that faith in the three major Hindu deities can give people strength and comfort during troubled times.
notes_20240423113814.simpleHindiExplanation: दोहा ब्रह्मा, विष्णु और महेश को जगत के पालनहार मानते हुए उनकी उपासना से क्लेश दूर होने का भक्तिपूर्ण विश्वास व्यक्त करता है।
notes_20240423113814.context: The prompt is “क्लेश.” The verse uses the Hindu triad of Brahma, Vishnu, and Mahesh to express a devotional belief about relief from distress.

literalEnglish: By damaging the environment, people are becoming ill.
Nature is pleading with us: use her resources responsibly.
notes_20240423113821.childFriendlyEnglish: If people harm nature or use too much, their own health suffers. The poem asks us to take only what we need and care for the environment.
notes_20240423113821.simpleHindiExplanation: पर्यावरण को बिगाड़ने से मनुष्य स्वयं बीमार हो रहा है। प्रकृति मानो विनती कर रही है कि उसके संसाधनों का सही और संतुलित उपयोग किया जाए।
notes_20240423113821.context: The 2022 record uses the prompt “रुग्ण” and directly links human illness with environmental damage and consumption. It is an environmental warning, not a claim about one specific incident.

literalEnglish: Chandrayaan's success is resounding everywhere.
See India's shining mark upon the moon, near its southern edge.
notes_20240423125044.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem celebrates India's moon mission and the pride people felt when Chandrayaan reached the lunar south-polar region.
notes_20240423125044.simpleHindiExplanation: यह दोहा चंद्रयान की सफलता पर उत्साह और राष्ट्रीय गर्व व्यक्त करता है। चाँद के दक्षिणी क्षेत्र में भारत की उपलब्धि को चमकते चिह्न के रूप में देखा गया है।
notes_20240423125044.context: Dated 2023-08-24, the day after Chandrayaan-3's announced lunar landing, the poem appears to celebrate that mission and its landing in the Moon's south-polar region. The preserved prompt is “चिह्न.”

literalEnglish: The world accepted Modi's proposal.
Yoga Day has now become a symbol of India's identity.
notes_20240423123457.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem celebrates the worldwide observance of Yoga Day and connects it with India's contribution to global well-being.
notes_20240423123457.simpleHindiExplanation: दोहा योग दिवस को विश्व स्तर पर स्वीकार किए जाने और उससे भारत की पहचान जुड़ने पर गर्व व्यक्त करता है। पहली पंक्ति इस पहल को नरेंद्र मोदी के प्रस्ताव से जोड़ती है।
notes_20240423123457.context: The record is dated 2023-06-21, International Day of Yoga, and names “योग” as the prompt. It appears to refer to the international adoption of Yoga Day following a proposal presented by Indian prime minister Narendra Modi.

literalEnglish: World Cup matches carry a distinctive excitement of their own.
Everyone watches India and Pakistan, placing their bets and predictions.
notes_20240423125321.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem captures the special excitement around an India–Pakistan World Cup match, when viewers eagerly guess which team will win.
notes_20240423125321.simpleHindiExplanation: यह दोहा विश्व कप में भारत-पाकिस्तान मुकाबले के अलग उत्साह को दिखाता है। लोग मैच देखते हुए जीत-हार पर शर्त या अनुमान लगाते हैं।
notes_20240423125321.context: Dated 2023-10-12, the poem appears to anticipate the India–Pakistan match in the 2023 Cricket World Cup. The exact sense of “शर्त” may range from informal predictions to literal betting.

literalEnglish: The whole country was absorbed, every eye fixed on the television.
When the World Cup was lost, everyone's peace of mind disappeared.
notes_20240423130256.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem remembers how closely people across India watched the World Cup final and how disappointed they felt after the loss.
notes_20240423130256.simpleHindiExplanation: पूरा देश टीवी पर विश्व कप का मुकाबला तन्मय होकर देख रहा था। हार के बाद लोगों की निराशा और बेचैनी को दूसरी पंक्ति व्यक्त करती है।
notes_20240423130256.context: Dated 2023-11-23, shortly after the 2023 men's Cricket World Cup final, the poem appears to reflect India's widespread disappointment after losing that final.

literalEnglish: People have grown deeply attached to the mobile phone.
Meanwhile, family ties and relationships are being left behind and losing importance.
notes_20240423123137.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem warns that spending too much attention on a phone can make us neglect the real people and relationships around us.
notes_20240423123137.simpleHindiExplanation: मनुष्य का लगाव मोबाइल से इतना बढ़ गया है कि रिश्ते-नाते पीछे छूट रहे हैं। दोहा तकनीक के कारण मानवीय संबंधों का महत्व कम होने की चेतावनी देता है।
notes_20240423123137.context: The 2023 poem uses “महत्त्व” as its prompt and comments on mobile-phone attachment. It is a general social observation rather than a reference to one identified event.

literalEnglish: The Constitution has given rights to the people.
To govern the nation, they choose their own government.
The Constitution means that everyone is equal.
There must be one law for people of every caste.
notes_20240423131041.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem explains that the Constitution gives citizens rights, lets them choose a government, and promises equal law for people of every caste.
notes_20240423131041.simpleHindiExplanation: रचना बताती है कि संविधान जनता को अधिकार और अपनी सरकार चुनने की शक्ति देता है। उसका मूल संदेश समानता है—हर जाति के लिए कानून एक समान होना चाहिए।
notes_20240423131041.context: The record is dated 2024-01-26, India's Republic Day, and names “संविधान” as the prompt. The poem focuses on democratic choice, rights, legal equality, and caste equality.

literalEnglish: In love, Shraddha forgot the honour due to her family.
She was cut into thirty-five pieces; her life was lost in vain.
notes_20240423113827.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem warns that intense attachment should not make someone ignore family concern or personal safety, and it mourns a young woman's violent death.
notes_20240423113827.simpleHindiExplanation: यह दोहा श्रद्धा नाम की युवती की हिंसक मृत्यु पर शोक व्यक्त करते हुए कहता है कि प्रेम में परिवार के सम्मान, सलाह और अपनी सुरक्षा को नहीं भूलना चाहिए।
notes_20240423113827.context: Dated 2022-11-16 with the prompt “सम्मान,” the wording “पैंतिस टुकड़े” appears to refer to the widely reported Shraddha Walkar murder case. This identification is an editorial inference from the date, name, and wording, not a statement of confirmed authorial intent.

literalEnglish: For a happy life, work wholeheartedly.
When the body grows tired, give it rest.
notes_20240423113833.childFriendlyEnglish: Work helps us build a good life, but rest is also necessary when our bodies become tired.
notes_20240423113833.simpleHindiExplanation: सुखी जीवन के लिए परिश्रम जरूरी है, लेकिन थक जाने पर शरीर को पर्याप्त आराम देना भी उतना ही जरूरी है।
notes_20240423113833.context: The preserved record is dated 2022-11-29 and names “आराम” as the prompt. Its advice balances diligent work with necessary physical rest; no specific external event is indicated.

literalEnglish: A powerful argument was made in favour of Ram Lalla.
Lawyer Parasaran had conducted the arguments and appeal.
notes_20240423113838.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem remembers the strong legal arguments made for Ram Lalla during the long court dispute about the Ayodhya site.
notes_20240423113838.simpleHindiExplanation: दोहा रामलला के पक्ष में दी गई मजबूत कानूनी दलीलों और वकील पाराशरण की भूमिका को याद करता है।
notes_20240423113838.context: Dated 2022-12-02 with “जिरह” as the prompt, the verse appears to refer to senior advocate K. Parasaran's arguments in the Ayodhya title case. The compact second line is grammatically compressed, so the exact distinction between argument and appeal remains uncertain.

literalEnglish: 7 December 2022
The scent of the people's verdict spread from television channels.
Lotuses bloomed in Gujarat, and their fragrance began to spread.
notes_20240423113847.childFriendlyEnglish: Using the lotus as an election symbol and a flower, the poem anticipates or celebrates news of a BJP victory in Gujarat.
notes_20240423113847.simpleHindiExplanation: टीवी पर चुनावी जनादेश की खबर फैलने और गुजरात में कमल खिलने की छवि के माध्यम से भाजपा की जीत का संकेत दिया गया है।
notes_20240423113847.context: The embedded date is 2022-12-07, one day before the announced Gujarat Assembly election results. “कमल” appears to work both as a flower and the BJP election symbol; because the result was not yet formally declared on that date, the wording may reflect exit-poll coverage or anticipation.

literalEnglish: Composition dated 8 December 2022
Do not be afraid when you see a moonless night.
The light of a lamp will destroy the darkness.
notes_20240423113858.childFriendlyEnglish: Even a small light can overcome a dark night, so we should keep hope when circumstances feel frightening.
notes_20240423113858.simpleHindiExplanation: अमावस्या जैसी अँधेरी परिस्थिति से घबराने के बजाय आशा का छोटा-सा दीप जलाए रखने की सीख दी गई है, क्योंकि प्रकाश अँधेरा दूर कर सकता है।
notes_20240423113858.context: The preserved record and embedded heading are dated 2022-12-08. The lamp and moonless night form a general image of courage and hope; no particular event or मंच prompt is preserved.

literalEnglish: Composition dated 31 December 2022
The hare raced the tortoise and was defeated.
The patient tortoise kept moving and was embraced by victory.
notes_20240423113937.childFriendlyEnglish: Like the tortoise in the familiar fable, a person who moves steadily and patiently can succeed even without being the fastest.
notes_20240423113937.simpleHindiExplanation: कछुए और खरगोश की कथा के माध्यम से बताया गया है कि धैर्य और लगातार प्रयास से जीत मिल सकती है।
notes_20240423113937.context: Dated 2022-12-31 and titled “धीर,” the poem retells the familiar tortoise-and-hare fable to praise patient persistence. No specific contemporary event is suggested.

literalEnglish: Composition dated 31 December 2022
Adi Shankaracharya was a profoundly learned scholar.
Whoever debated scripture with him could not remain proud.
notes_20240423113951.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem praises Adi Shankaracharya's great learning and says that his skill in philosophical debate humbled his opponents.
notes_20240423113951.simpleHindiExplanation: आदि शंकराचार्य को महान विद्वान बताते हुए उनकी शास्त्रार्थ-कुशलता की प्रशंसा की गई है, जिसके सामने विरोधी का घमंड टिक नहीं पाता था।
notes_20240423113951.context: The preserved record is dated 2022-12-31 and titled “प्रकांड.” It invokes the traditional reputation of Adi Shankaracharya as a formidable scholar and debater; it does not identify one particular debate.

literalEnglish: Composition dated 31 December 2022
Speak only after careful thought, keeping patience in your mind.
Words do not return, just as an arrow does not return to the bow.
notes_20240423114012.childFriendlyEnglish: Think calmly before speaking, because hurtful words cannot simply be taken back once they have been said.
notes_20240423114012.simpleHindiExplanation: बोलने से पहले धैर्य रखकर सोचने की सीख है, क्योंकि मुँह से निकले शब्द कमान से छूटे तीर की तरह वापस नहीं आते।
notes_20240423114012.context: Dated 2022-12-31 and titled “धीर,” the verse uses the familiar arrow metaphor to offer general advice about patient, responsible speech.

literalEnglish: Composition dated 31 December 2022
Learn from the spider, which keeps patience in its heart.
Even after falling, it tries again and does not become restless.
notes_20240423114021.childFriendlyEnglish: A spider rebuilds and keeps trying after it falls, reminding us not to give up when our first attempt fails.
notes_20240423114021.simpleHindiExplanation: मकड़ी बार-बार गिरकर भी जाला बनाने का प्रयास करती है। उससे धैर्य, हिम्मत और असफलता के बाद फिर कोशिश करने की सीख मिलती है।
notes_20240423114021.context: Dated 2022-12-31 and titled “धीर,” the poem draws a moral lesson from a spider's repeated effort. It is a general perseverance image rather than a dated public reference.

literalEnglish: Composition dated 5 January 2023
The sun god rides his chariot—what remarkable horses!
They are said to have become the seven days of the week.
notes_20240423114026.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem connects Surya's chariot and its seven horses with the seven days of the week, using a traditional mythic image.
notes_20240423114026.simpleHindiExplanation: सूर्य देव के रथ के सात घोड़ों को सप्ताह के सात दिनों से जोड़कर पौराणिक कल्पना प्रस्तुत की गई है।
notes_20240423114026.context: The embedded date is 2023-01-05 and the title is “रथ.” The seven horses of Surya's chariot are a traditional Hindu image; the line's link to the seven weekdays is poetic rather than a historical claim.

literalEnglish: Composition dated 5 January 2023
If a cat crosses your path, do not begin the journey.
If you meet a water-filled vessel, regard it as an auspicious sign.
notes_20240423114030.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem records two traditional journey omens: a cat crossing the path is treated as a warning, while a full water vessel is treated as fortunate.
notes_20240423114030.simpleHindiExplanation: दोहा यात्रा से जुड़ी लोकमान्यताओं को दर्ज करता है—बिल्ली का रास्ता काटना अशुभ और जल से भरा कलश मिलना शुभ माना गया है।
notes_20240423114030.context: The embedded date is 2023-01-05 and the title is “शुभ.” The verse presents traditional omen beliefs; the editorial layer records those beliefs without asserting that they predict real outcomes.

literalEnglish: Composition dated 4 January 2023
The fierce goddess Chandika struck the demon Raktabija.
So that his blood would not fall on the ground, she drank it and destroyed him.
notes_20240423114101.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem recalls the goddess's battle with Raktabija, whose spilled blood could create more demons, and how she stopped it from reaching the ground.
notes_20240423114101.simpleHindiExplanation: देवी चंडिका और रक्तबीज की पौराणिक कथा का वर्णन है। रक्तबीज का रक्त धरती पर गिरकर नए दैत्य न बनाए, इसलिए देवी ने उसका रक्त पीकर उसका संहार किया।
notes_20240423114101.context: The embedded date is 2023-01-04 and the title is “रक्त.” The wording clearly draws on the Devi Mahatmya tradition concerning the battle against Raktabija.

literalEnglish: The holy man is deceiving people, while television gives him publicity.
A mantra is presented as the cure for every illness, making doctors seem useless.
notes_20240423114107.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem criticizes televised miracle claims that promise to cure every disease with a mantra and dismiss the value of doctors.
notes_20240423114107.simpleHindiExplanation: टीवी प्रचार के सहारे हर रोग को मंत्र से ठीक करने का दावा करने वाले बाबा पर व्यंग्य है। दोहा ऐसे दावों से सावधान रहने और चिकित्सा को बेकार न समझने का संकेत देता है।
notes_20240423114107.context: The record was saved on 2023-01-22, carries an internal date of 2023-01-23, and names “चकमा” as the prompt. It appears to satirize televised faith-healing claims; no individual is named, so identifying a specific person would be uncertain.

literalEnglish: Composition dated 22 January 2023
Why do you cut down forests and woods? Listen, foolish human.
Animals have lost their homes, and the world has grown fiercely hot.
notes_20240423114112.childFriendlyEnglish: Cutting forests destroys animals' homes and makes the climate hotter, so people must protect trees and habitats.
notes_20240423114112.simpleHindiExplanation: वनों की कटाई से जीवों का घर छिनता है और गर्मी बढ़ती है। दोहा मनुष्य को जंगल बचाने की कड़ी चेतावनी देता है।
notes_20240423114112.context: The embedded date is 2023-01-22 and the title is “वन.” The wording directly connects deforestation with habitat loss and severe heat, without pointing to one named incident.

literalEnglish: Composition dated 22 January 2023
Consider every ‘but’ and ‘however’ before undertaking a task.
Resolve your doubts, and you will reach your destination.
notes_20240423114116.childFriendlyEnglish: Before starting important work, think through your questions and difficulties so that you can move toward your goal with clarity.
notes_20240423114116.simpleHindiExplanation: कोई काम करने से पहले किंतु-परंतु और शंकाओं पर विचार करके उनका समाधान करना चाहिए; इससे लक्ष्य तक पहुँचना आसान होता है।
notes_20240423114116.context: The embedded date is 2023-01-22 and the title is “परंतु.” The poem turns conjunctions expressing hesitation into practical advice about planning and resolving doubts.

literalEnglish: Composition dated 23 January 2023
The sun blossoms in the east, and dawn spreads across the sky.
Birds call and chirp in every direction.
notes_20240423114121.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem paints a cheerful morning scene as the sun rises and birds fill the sky with their calls.
notes_20240423114121.simpleHindiExplanation: पूर्व दिशा में सूर्योदय, आकाश में भोर और चारों ओर पक्षियों के कलरव का सुंदर प्रातःकालीन दृश्य प्रस्तुत किया गया है।
notes_20240423114121.context: The embedded date is 2023-01-23 and the title is “नभ.” The imagery is a general observation of dawn and birdsong, with no identifiable external event.

literalEnglish: Subhas / Netaji / the Indian freedom army
Composition dated 23 January 2023
Subhas asked for blood for the sake of freedom.
He formed an Indian army, and the world became a bridge.
notes_20240423114126.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem honours Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose, recalling his call for sacrifice and the formation of the Indian National Army in the struggle for freedom.
notes_20240423114126.simpleHindiExplanation: नेताजी सुभाष चंद्र बोस के प्रसिद्ध आह्वान और आजाद हिंद फौज के निर्माण को याद करते हुए स्वतंत्रता संग्राम में उनके योगदान का सम्मान किया गया है।
notes_20240423114126.context: The embedded date, 2023-01-23, is Subhas Chandra Bose's birth anniversary. The phrases about giving blood and forming an army clearly evoke his famous call and the Azad Hind Fauj; the final “world became a bridge” image is less precise and may suggest international connections or support.

literalEnglish: Composition dated 13 October 2023
The first invitation makes the whole setting auspicious.
My chosen deity is Ganesha, the son of Gauri.
notes_20240423114130.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem expresses devotion to Ganesha and recalls the custom of honouring him first so that an occasion begins auspiciously.
notes_20240423114130.simpleHindiExplanation: गौरीपुत्र गणेश को आराध्य मानते हुए किसी शुभ कार्य या निमंत्रण में सबसे पहले उनका स्मरण करने की परंपरा व्यक्त की गई है।
notes_20240423114130.context: The record is ordered under 2023-01-23, but its preserved body contains “13/10/2023,” an internal date inconsistency that is left unresolved. The verse reflects the customary first invocation of Ganesha at auspicious beginnings.

literalEnglish: Composition dated 21 January 2023
Life began with crying; may it end with laughter.
With attention fixed at the Lord's feet, may life become spring.
notes_20240423114134.childFriendlyEnglish: Although life starts with a baby's cry, the poem hopes it will grow joyful and spiritually peaceful through devotion.
notes_20240423114134.simpleHindiExplanation: जीवन जन्म के रोने से शुरू होता है, पर अंत हँसी और संतोष से हो—यह कामना है। प्रभु-भक्ति से जीवन को बसंत जैसा सुखद बनाने का भाव है।
notes_20240423114134.context: The embedded date is 2023-01-21 and the title is “प्रारंभ.” The poem combines the human life cycle with devotional imagery; it does not identify a particular ceremony or event.

literalEnglish: Composition dated 20 January 2023
The women wrestlers are revealing hidden matters.
If they protest with awakened resolve, all will come to their senses.
notes_20240423114137.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem supports women wrestlers who spoke publicly and protested, suggesting that their courage could force wrongdoers or authorities to respond.
notes_20240423114137.simpleHindiExplanation: अपनी शिकायतें सामने लाकर धरना देने वाली महिला पहलवानों के साहस और जागरूकता का समर्थन किया गया है। अंतिम वाक्य का भाव है कि विरोध से जिम्मेदार लोग सुधरेंगे या पीछे हटेंगे।
notes_20240423114137.context: The embedded date is 2023-01-20, during the January 2023 protest by leading Indian women wrestlers. The wording appears to refer to that protest, although it does not name the allegations, officials, or organizations involved.

literalEnglish: Composition dated 19 January 2023
In Baladau's hand, the plough serves as a weapon.
His wondrous weapon keeps enemies in distress.
notes_20240423114203.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem describes Balarama, also called Baladau, carrying his famous plough as a powerful weapon.
notes_20240423114203.simpleHindiExplanation: बलदाऊ अर्थात बलराम के हाथ में हल को अस्त्र के रूप में दिखाया गया है, जिससे उनके शत्रु भयभीत रहते हैं।
notes_20240423114203.context: The embedded date is 2023-01-19 and the title is “हल.” “बलदाऊ” is a familiar name for Balarama, whose plough is a well-known attribute in Hindu tradition.

literalEnglish: Composition dated 17 January 2023
King Dhritarashtra's judgment became blind.
What happened in the gambling court was not a righteous step.
notes_20240423114208.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem says Dhritarashtra failed to judge rightly during the Mahabharata dice-game assembly, using blindness as a moral as well as physical image.
notes_20240423114208.simpleHindiExplanation: महाभारत के द्यूत-सभा प्रसंग में धृतराष्ट्र के विवेकहीन और अन्यायपूर्ण निर्णय की आलोचना की गई है। यहाँ अंधापन नैतिक विवेक के अभाव का भी संकेत है।
notes_20240423114208.context: The embedded date is 2023-01-17 and the title is “अंधा.” The wording clearly invokes Dhritarashtra and the Mahabharata dice-game court; it is a mythological moral judgment, not a claim about a current event.

literalEnglish: Composition dated 18 January 2023
Truth is being murdered while people stand silent.
They use the Gita while speaking lies.
notes_20240423114212.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem condemns people who stay silent when truth is harmed and who misuse a sacred book to support false statements.
notes_20240423114212.simpleHindiExplanation: सत्य के दबने पर लोगों की चुप्पी और झूठ बोलते समय गीता का सहारा लेने की विडंबना पर तीखी आलोचना की गई है।
notes_20240423114212.context: The embedded date is 2023-01-18 and the title is “हत्या.” The killing of truth is metaphorical, and the Gita reference appears to criticize false swearing or religious hypocrisy; no specific case is named.

literalEnglish: Music flows from waterfalls, birds, and trees.
A fragrant, gentle breeze blows, and nature expresses love.
notes_20240423114216.childFriendlyEnglish: The sounds of water, birds, leaves, and a soft breeze come together like nature's own loving music.
notes_20240423114216.simpleHindiExplanation: झरनों, पक्षियों, पेड़ों और सुगंधित मंद हवा की ध्वनियों को प्रकृति के मधुर संगीत और प्रेम के रूप में देखा गया है।
notes_20240423114216.context: The record is dated 2023-01-23 and its raw heading includes “दोहा 19/1/2023.” The verse is a nature scene built around sound, fragrance, and breeze; no specific location is preserved.

literalEnglish: Composition dated 21 January 2023
Never take photographs; keep charitable giving private.
If someone's dignity is hurt, the merit of the gift will disappear.
notes_20240423114221.childFriendlyEnglish: When helping someone, do it quietly instead of using their need for a photograph, because their dignity matters more than praise.
notes_20240423114221.simpleHindiExplanation: दान का दिखावा या फोटो खिंचवाने से जरूरतमंद का सम्मान आहत हो सकता है। इसलिए सहायता गुप्त और गरिमा बनाए रखते हुए करनी चाहिए।
notes_20240423114221.context: The embedded date is 2023-01-21 and the title is “गुप्त.” The poem applies a traditional ideal of private charity to the modern practice of photographing donations.

literalEnglish: Composition dated 18 January 2023
Faith was wounded through years of fighting the court case.
Seeing the temple being built brings special joy.
notes_20240423114225.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem describes the pain of a long legal dispute and the happiness felt by devotees when they saw a temple under construction.
notes_20240423114225.simpleHindiExplanation: लंबे मुकदमे से आस्था को लगी चोट और मंदिर निर्माण देखकर मिली विशेष खुशी का भाव व्यक्त किया गया है।
notes_20240423114225.context: The embedded date is 2023-01-18. In proximity to the batch's Ram Lalla and Ayodhya references, “मंदिर” and the long court case appear to indicate the Ram temple at Ayodhya, but the poem itself does not name the site.

literalEnglish: Composition dated 17 January 2023
A mother's affection is shade; a father's stern strength is sunlight.
Both are necessary, according to the occasion.
notes_20240423114229.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem compares a mother's comfort to cool shade and a father's firmness to sunlight, saying children may need both kinds of care.
notes_20240423114229.simpleHindiExplanation: माँ की ममता को छाँव और पिता के तेज या अनुशासन को धूप कहा गया है। परिस्थिति के अनुसार बच्चों के जीवन में दोनों की जरूरत बताई गई है।
notes_20240423114229.context: The embedded date is 2023-01-17 and the title is “धूप.” The verse uses contrasting weather images to describe parental roles; these are poetic generalizations rather than claims about every family.

literalEnglish: Composition dated 16 January 2023
In the shelter of one's parents, one senses an ancient banyan.
Its dense, cool shade is found there, while storms remain far away.
notes_20240423114234.childFriendlyEnglish: Parents are compared to a strong banyan tree whose broad shade gives children comfort, protection, and a feeling of safety.
notes_20240423114234.simpleHindiExplanation: माता-पिता की शरण को बरगद की घनी, शीतल छाँव जैसा बताया गया है, जो संतान को सुरक्षा और कठिनाइयों से बचाव का भरोसा देती है।
notes_20240423114234.context: The embedded date is 2023-01-16 and the title is “छांव.” The banyan and storm imagery offers a general metaphor for parental protection.

literalEnglish: Composition dated 20 January 2023
After learning about an inauspicious direction, undertake the journey
with careful thought.
Consult astrological calculations, and you will cross safely.
notes_20240423114239.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem records the traditional belief that travellers should check directional omens and astrology before setting out.
notes_20240423114239.simpleHindiExplanation: यात्रा से पहले दिशा-शूल और ज्योतिषीय गणना देखने की पारंपरिक मान्यता बताई गई है, ताकि सफर शुभ और सुरक्षित माना जाए।
notes_20240423114239.context: The embedded date is 2023-01-20 and the title is “यात्रा.” “दिशा शूल” is a traditional astrological travel restriction; this editorial explanation records the belief without presenting it as scientifically verified guidance.

literalEnglish: Composition dated 14 January 2023
Many kinds of people stand upon the stage of politics.
Those who obtain power proceed to misuse it.
notes_20240423114243.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem warns that political power can attract many different people and may be abused by those who gain it.
notes_20240423114243.simpleHindiExplanation: राजनीति में अनेक प्रकार के लोग आते हैं और सत्ता मिलने पर कुछ लोग उसका दुरुपयोग करते हैं—दोहा इसी प्रवृत्ति की आलोचना करता है।
notes_20240423114243.context: The embedded date is 2023-01-14 and the title is “मंच.” The criticism is broad and does not identify a party, officeholder, or particular incident.

literalEnglish: Composition dated 24 January 2023
When it is confirmed that one has passed the examination,
the heart feels happiness and gains satisfaction.
notes_20240423114247.childFriendlyEnglish: Waiting for exam results can be tense, and confirmed success brings both happiness and relief.
notes_20240423114247.simpleHindiExplanation: परीक्षा में सफलता की पुष्टि होने पर मन में खुशी, राहत और संतुष्टि आने का सरल अनुभव व्यक्त किया गया है।
notes_20240423114247.context: The record was saved on 2023-01-23 while its body is dated 2023-01-24. The title “संतुष्टि” and wording concern a general examination result; no particular exam is named.

literalEnglish: Composition dated 25 January 2023
God's presence exists throughout the whole animate and inanimate world.
As the supreme seed, God brings the world's creation into being.
notes_20240423114251.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem sees the divine in every living and non-living part of the universe and imagines God as the seed from which creation grows.
notes_20240423114251.simpleHindiExplanation: समस्त जड़-चेतन जगत में ईश्वर की उपस्थिति मानी गई है और उन्हें सृष्टि के मूल बीज तथा रचयिता के रूप में देखा गया है।
notes_20240423114251.context: The record is dated 2023-01-24 and its body carries 2023-01-25. The title “चराचर” frames a devotional reflection on divine presence throughout creation.

literalEnglish: Topic: “Powerful”
29 January 2023
The person who becomes powerful is the one who wins.
Whoever holds the stick gets to own the buffalo.
The buffalo is his indeed, especially if he is a minister.
The police become flatterers and never miss an opportunity.
An officer goes searching, taking a whole squad along.
They find the buffalo, bring it back, and tie it to the post.
Respectfully submitted for review.
notes_20240423114258.childFriendlyEnglish: With humour about a minister's missing buffalo, the poem says powerful people can make police and officials serve their private interests.
notes_20240423114258.simpleHindiExplanation: मंत्री की भैंस खोजने में पुलिस और अफसरों के जुट जाने की हास्यपूर्ण कल्पना से सत्ता, चापलूसी और सरकारी साधनों के निजी उपयोग पर व्यंग्य किया गया है।
notes_20240423114258.context: The record was saved on 2023-01-25, identifies “समर्थ” as the topic, and contains a line dated 2023-01-29. The minister-and-buffalo episode may echo reported political anecdotes, but no person, place, or specific incident is named, so that link remains uncertain.

literalEnglish: Topic: “In accordance”
21 January 2023
Listen to the pleading call of forests and mountains.
Learn from Joshimath and live in accordance with nature.
Live in accordance with nature, whose creator is God.
Nature is growing angry; observe its balance.
Do not grow arrogantly tall; seek well-being beneath the mountains.
You caused destruction by laying waste to trees and forests.
Respectfully submitted for review.
notes_20240423114305.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem points to Joshimath's crisis as a warning that construction and tree loss in the mountains must respect nature's limits.
notes_20240423114305.simpleHindiExplanation: जोशीमठ की स्थिति से सीख लेकर पहाड़, जंगल और प्रकृति के संतुलन के अनुसार विकास करने की चेतावनी दी गई है। पेड़ों और वनों के विनाश को संकट का कारण माना गया है।
notes_20240423114305.context: The record was saved on 2023-01-25, names “अनुसार” as the topic, and includes 2023-01-21 in its body. Its direct mention of Joshimath appears to refer to the land-subsidence crisis prominent in January 2023; the poem's causal language is an environmental interpretation, not a technical geological assessment.

literalEnglish: The tradition of Raghu's line is to keep a promise even at the cost of life.
In the present age the reverse occurs, as friends look to self-interest.
notes_20240423114309.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem contrasts the ideal of keeping one's word at any cost with friendships that change whenever selfish benefit is involved.
notes_20240423114309.simpleHindiExplanation: रघुकुल की वचन-पालन परंपरा की तुलना आज के स्वार्थपूर्ण संबंधों से की गई है, जहाँ मित्र भी अपना लाभ देखकर साथ देते हैं।
notes_20240423114309.context: The raw note identifies 2023-01-13 and “वचन” as the prompt, although the catalog record is dated 2023-01-25. “रघुकुल” invokes the traditional ideal associated with Rama's lineage; the criticism of the present age is general.

literalEnglish: King Kubera, a Yaksha, is the deity of wealth and splendour.
He lives in Alakapuri, in a home heaped with riches.
notes_20240423114313.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem introduces Kubera, the mythological lord of wealth, and his splendid city Alakapuri.
notes_20240423114313.simpleHindiExplanation: यक्षराज कुबेर को धन और वैभव का देवता बताते हुए उनके अलकापुरी में निवास का पौराणिक वर्णन किया गया है।
notes_20240423114313.context: The catalog record is dated 2023-01-25, while the raw note also preserves “1/10/2023,” so its exact composition date is uncertain. The prompt is “यक्ष,” and the references to Kubera and Alakapuri are clearly mythological.

literalEnglish: Salutations to the Doha Dhurandhar forum.
Prepare fifty-six offerings and place a tulsi leaf upon them.
Nothing compares with tulsi; it makes the offering complete.
notes_20240423114317.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem says that even a grand food offering becomes complete through the simple, sacred addition of a tulsi leaf.
notes_20240423114317.simpleHindiExplanation: छप्पन भोग जैसे बड़े प्रसाद में भी तुलसी-दल को अनिवार्य और अनुपम माना गया है; उसकी सादगी भोग को पूर्ण करती है।
notes_20240423114317.context: The raw note preserves 2022-12-26 and “तुलसी” as the prompt, though the catalog record is dated 2023-01-25. The verse reflects a Vaishnava devotional custom of placing tulsi leaves on food offerings.

literalEnglish: The holy man performs miracles, leaving everyone's mind astonished.
Without medicine, he claims to diagnose and cure disease through mantras.
notes_20240423114321.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem sounds skeptical of a holy man's surprising claim that mantras can diagnose and cure illnesses without medicine.
notes_20240423114321.simpleHindiExplanation: बिना दवा केवल मंत्र से रोग का निदान या इलाज करने वाले बाबा के चमत्कारी दावे पर आश्चर्य और व्यंग्य व्यक्त किया गया है।
notes_20240423114321.context: The raw note is dated 2023-01-24 and gives “मति” as the prompt. Read alongside nearby poems about televised miracle cures, it appears satirical, but the wording could also be read as wonder; no particular claimant is named.

literalEnglish: People have continued to be martyred while defending the nation.
The brave Abdul Hamid gave his life in sacrifice for the country.
Respectfully submitted for review.
notes_20240423114329.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem honours soldiers who died protecting India and specifically remembers the courage and sacrifice of Abdul Hamid.
notes_20240423114329.simpleHindiExplanation: देश की रक्षा में शहीद हुए सैनिकों को नमन करते हुए परमवीर चक्र विजेता अब्दुल हमीद के बलिदान को विशेष रूप से याद किया गया है।
notes_20240423114329.context: Dated 2023-01-25 with “शहीद” as the prompt, the poem names Abdul Hamid, the Indian soldier remembered for his actions and death in the 1965 India–Pakistan war. The verse is commemorative rather than a reference to a new 2023 event.

literalEnglish: The whole world is false; no true friend is found here.
Love God, and you will have no fear of worldly existence.
notes_20240423114334.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem expresses a devotional belief that worldly relationships may disappoint us, while love for God can ease fear and insecurity.
notes_20240423114334.simpleHindiExplanation: सांसारिक संबंधों को अस्थिर मानते हुए भगवान से प्रेम करने की सीख दी गई है, ताकि भवसागर या जीवन के भय से मुक्ति का भरोसा मिले।
notes_20240423114334.context: The raw note is dated 2023-01-25 and names “नेह” as the prompt. Its contrast between the unreliable world and divine love belongs to a familiar devotional tradition; it is not evidence about a particular relationship.

literalEnglish: Performance
The holy man is putting on a show, and all the people are spectators.
He claims that grace removes every illness without medicine.
Respectfully submitted for review.
notes_20240423114338.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem compares a miracle healer's claims to a stage show, with the public watching promises that every disease can vanish without medicine.
notes_20240423114338.simpleHindiExplanation: बिना दवा कृपा से हर रोग दूर करने के दावे को नाटक या नौटंकी बताकर चमत्कारी उपचार और उसे देखने वाली भीड़ पर व्यंग्य किया गया है।
notes_20240423114338.context: Dated 2023-01-24 with “नाटक/नौटंकी” as the prompt, the poem appears to criticize public miracle-healing performances. It does not name an individual or establish whether one particular broadcast prompted it.

literalEnglish: Courage
The women wrestlers are fighting courageously.
Sitting in protest, they are revealing hidden matters.
notes_20240423114342.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem praises women wrestlers for courageously protesting and speaking about matters that had been kept hidden.
notes_20240423114342.simpleHindiExplanation: धरने पर बैठकर अपनी शिकायतें और छिपी बातें सामने लाने वाली महिला पहलवानों के साहस की प्रशंसा की गई है।
notes_20240423114342.context: Dated 2023-01-20 with “साहस/शौर्य” as the prompt, the wording appears to refer to the January 2023 protest by prominent Indian women wrestlers. The poem does not specify the allegations or identify those accused.

literalEnglish: Topic: Astonishment
One is astonished to see the ways of dishonest people.
They act sweet outwardly but hold no affection within.
With no affection within, they say only what pleases the powerful.
How shamelessly stubborn they are; they feel no embarrassment.
They become acquainted with you to fulfil their self-interest.
Keep your distance from them; do not be surprised by them.
notes_20240423114346.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem warns that dishonest flatterers may speak sweetly only to gain something, so notice their actions and keep a sensible distance.
notes_20240423114346.simpleHindiExplanation: बेईमान और स्वार्थी लोग बाहर से मीठा बोलते हैं, मन में सच्चा प्रेम नहीं रखते और लाभ के लिए खुशामद करते हैं। उनसे सावधानी और दूरी रखने की सलाह दी गई है।
notes_20240423114346.context: The catalog record is dated 2023-01-25 and the preserved topic is “विस्मय.” The kundaliya-style verse offers broad social advice about flattery and self-serving relationships, without naming a person or event.

literalEnglish: The elders of a household are like an ancient banyan tree.
Noble children remain beneath their shade.
notes_20240423114352.childFriendlyEnglish: Older family members are compared to a long-lived banyan tree whose shade offers younger generations guidance and protection.
notes_20240423114352.simpleHindiExplanation: घर के बुजुर्गों को प्राचीन बरगद की तरह सम्मान और संरक्षण देने वाला बताया गया है; संस्कारी संतान उनके स्नेह और मार्गदर्शन की छाँव में रहती है।
notes_20240423114352.context: Dated 2023-01-26 with “प्राचीन” as the prompt, the poem uses the banyan tree as a family metaphor. “कुलीन” is interpreted here as well-brought-up or noble in conduct, not as a verified social status.

literalEnglish: The spring season has spread everywhere, filling the heart with emotion.
The cuckoo calls from the mango tree, and flowers bloom all around.
notes_20240423114356.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem welcomes spring with blooming flowers and a cuckoo singing from a mango tree.
notes_20240423114356.simpleHindiExplanation: बसंत के आगमन से मन प्रसन्न और भाव-विभोर है। आम के पेड़ पर कोयल की कूक और चारों ओर खिले फूल ऋतु का सुंदर दृश्य बनाते हैं।
notes_20240423114356.context: Dated 2023-01-26 with “बसंत” as the prompt, the poem uses familiar North Indian spring imagery. It does not identify a particular garden or observation site.

literalEnglish: Vasant Panchami
On the fifth day of spring, Saraswati appeared.
Take refuge in her and choose the path of knowledge.
Respectfully submitted for review.
notes_20240423114401.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem celebrates Vasant Panchami by honouring Saraswati and encouraging learners to seek her blessing and choose knowledge.
notes_20240423114401.simpleHindiExplanation: बसंत पंचमी पर देवी सरस्वती के अवतरण का स्मरण करते हुए उनकी शरण में जाकर ज्ञान अपनाने की प्रेरणा दी गई है।
notes_20240423114401.context: Dated 2023-01-26 with the combined prompt “बसंत पंचमी/गणतंत्र दिवस,” this verse chooses the Vasant Panchami subject and invokes Saraswati as the goddess of learning.

literalEnglish: India is a republic, and we are proud of it.
Governance now operates according to the Constitution's principles.
notes_20240423114407.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem expresses pride that India is a republic governed through the Constitution rather than the rule of a monarch.
notes_20240423114407.simpleHindiExplanation: भारत के गणतंत्र होने पर गर्व व्यक्त किया गया है और कहा गया है कि देश का शासन संविधान की नीतियों के अनुसार चलता है।
notes_20240423114407.context: The record was saved on Republic Day, 2023-01-26, while its raw note gives 2023-01-27 and names “गणतंत्र” as the prompt. The verse directly concerns India's constitutional republic.

literalEnglish: Song / Music
On hearing Baiju's song, everyone forgot their hostility.
Tansen gave up his pride and prayed to God for well-being.
notes_20240423114411.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem recalls the legendary singers Baiju and Tansen, imagining music so powerful that it ends rivalry and humbles pride.
notes_20240423114411.simpleHindiExplanation: बैजू बावरा और तानसेन से जुड़ी लोकप्रचलित कथा के सहारे संगीत की शक्ति दिखाई गई है—गीत बैर मिटाता है और अहंकार को विनम्रता में बदल देता है।
notes_20240423114411.context: Dated 2023-01-27, the poem names song and music and appears to draw on popular legends of Baiju Bawra and Tansen. The precise episode varies across retellings, so the verse should not be treated as a documented historical account.

literalEnglish: With a sweet, cuckoo-like voice, the name Lata became famous.
Whenever I hear her songs, a feeling of enchantment spreads over me.
notes_20240423114417.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem lovingly praises Lata Mangeshkar's famously sweet voice and the spell her songs cast on the listener.
notes_20240423114417.simpleHindiExplanation: लता मंगेशकर की मधुर, कोयल जैसी आवाज की प्रशंसा है। उनके गीत सुनकर मन पर छाने वाले आनंद और सुरूर को व्यक्त किया गया है।
notes_20240423114417.context: Dated 2023-01-27 with “मधुर” as the prompt, “लता” and the famous sweet singing voice appear to refer to Lata Mangeshkar. The identification is strong from the wording, though her surname is not written.

literalEnglish: The sun, stars, and moon sparkle brightly in the sky.
Marigolds and roses bloom and spread fragrance in the garden.
A fragrant spring breeze flows, and birds chirp again and again.
Mango blossoms appear, and a cuckoo calls from the branch.
Respectfully submitted for review.
notes_20240423114433.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem gathers a bright sky, fragrant flowers, singing birds, mango blossoms, and a cuckoo into one joyful spring scene.
notes_20240423114433.simpleHindiExplanation: आकाश की चमक, बाग के गेंदे और गुलाब, सुगंधित बहार, चहकते पक्षी, आम के बौर और कोयल की कूक से बसंत का जीवंत चित्र बनाया गया है।
notes_20240423114433.context: Dated 2023-01-29 and identified as a rola-form composition, the poem presents seasonal nature imagery. No specific location, occasion, or external event is stated.

literalEnglish: With Rama beside her, Janaki rests peacefully in a hut.
In the royal palace, Urmila's eyes pour with tears.
notes_20240423114517.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem contrasts Sita's peace while sharing Rama's forest exile with Urmila's sorrow in the palace after Lakshmana has gone away.
notes_20240423114517.simpleHindiExplanation: सीता राम के साथ वन की कुटिया में रहकर भी संतोष पाती हैं, जबकि महल में रह गई उर्मिला लक्ष्मण के वियोग में रोती हैं। सुख केवल वैभव से नहीं, प्रिय के साथ से जुड़ा है।
notes_20240423114517.context: Dated 2023-01-29 with “कुटिया” as the prompt, the verse draws on the Ramayana exile: Janaki is Sita, and Urmila is Lakshmana's wife. The emotional contrast is clear, though the poem does not narrate the wider episode.

literalEnglish: One's own hut is better, for there one finds happiness and peace.
Friend, in another's palace neither day nor night passes easily.
notes_20240423114523.childFriendlyEnglish: A modest home of one's own can feel safer and happier than a grand palace where a person feels like an outsider.
notes_20240423114523.simpleHindiExplanation: अपनी छोटी-सी कुटिया में अपनापन और चैन मिलता है। किसी दूसरे के महल में बहुत सुविधा होते हुए भी परायापन हो तो दिन-रात काटना कठिन लगता है।
notes_20240423114523.context: Dated 2023-01-29 with “कुटिया” as the prompt, the poem contrasts belonging in a humble home with discomfort in someone else's palace. “सखी” is a conversational address, not evidence of a specific speaker or event.

literalEnglish: The name Prayag arose from Brahma's sacrificial rite.
Whoever enters this place sees their fortune awaken.
notes_20240423114621.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem presents Prayag as a sacred place linked with Brahma and says that visiting it can feel blessed and fortunate.
notes_20240423114621.simpleHindiExplanation: प्रयाग के नाम को ब्रह्मा के यज्ञ से जोड़ते हुए इस तीर्थ में प्रवेश को शुभ और भाग्य जगाने वाला माना गया है। यह धार्मिक आस्था का कथन है।
notes_20240423114621.context: Dated 2023-01-29 with “प्रयाग” as the prompt, the verse repeats a traditional sacred-origin association between Prayag and Brahma's yajna. The claim belongs to religious tradition rather than independently verified history.

literalEnglish: Whoever worships Narayan finds release from worldly existence.
Leave worldly entanglements and devote yourself to him.
notes_20240423114624.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem encourages devotion to Narayan as a path away from worldly worry and toward spiritual freedom.
notes_20240423114624.simpleHindiExplanation: नारायण की भक्ति को संसार के बंधनों से मुक्ति का मार्ग बताया गया है और दुनियावी उलझनों से ऊपर उठकर ईश्वर में मन लगाने की प्रेरणा दी गई है।
notes_20240423114624.context: The raw note gives 2023-01-30 and “नारायण” as the prompt, while the catalog date is 2023-01-29. The verse states a general Vaishnava devotional teaching; the dating discrepancy remains unresolved.

literalEnglish: Holding a flute to his lips, the stealer of Radha's heart appears.
Wearing a peacock-feather crown, young Krishna dances.
notes_20240423114628.childFriendlyEnglish: Krishna is pictured dancing with his flute and peacock-feather crown, charming Radha with his playful beauty.
notes_20240423114628.simpleHindiExplanation: कृष्ण के अधरों पर बाँसुरी, सिर पर मोर-मुकुट और नृत्य करती छवि का वर्णन है। उन्हें राधा का मन मोह लेने वाला नंदकिशोर कहा गया है।
notes_20240423114628.context: Dated 2023-01-30 with “मोर” as the prompt, the poem uses familiar Krishna imagery: flute, peacock-feather crown, Radha, and the name Nandkishore. It is devotional-poetic rather than a claim about a historical scene.

literalEnglish: Those known as steadfast people are like the sun.
Whether rising or setting, they remain the same.
notes_20240423114633.childFriendlyEnglish: A steady person keeps the same calm character in success and decline, just as the sun remains the sun at sunrise and sunset.
notes_20240423114633.simpleHindiExplanation: धीर व्यक्ति की तुलना सूर्य से की गई है। उन्नति हो या अवनति, वह अपना संतुलन और स्वभाव बनाए रखता है।
notes_20240423114633.context: Dated 2023-01-30 with “धीर/गंभीर” as the prompt, the verse uses sunrise and sunset metaphorically for changing circumstances. It gives general moral advice and names no particular person.

literalEnglish: The clay stove has become a memory of a bygone age.
The food had flavour, but fuel was wasted.
notes_20240423114637.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem remembers tasty food from traditional clay stoves while also noticing that they consumed a great deal of firewood or other fuel.
notes_20240423114637.simpleHindiExplanation: मिट्टी के पुराने चूल्हे और उस पर बने स्वादिष्ट भोजन को याद किया गया है, साथ ही यह भी माना गया है कि उसमें ईंधन अधिक खर्च होता था।
notes_20240423114637.context: Dated 2023-01-31 with “चूल्हा” as the prompt, the poem balances nostalgia for clay-stove cooking with concern about fuel use. It does not specify which fuel or household practice is meant.

literalEnglish: The gas stove arrived, and women welcomed it.
Recognize the life of trees and stop cutting them.
notes_20240423114641.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem welcomes cleaner, convenient gas cooking and connects it with saving trees that might otherwise be cut for fuel.
notes_20240423114641.simpleHindiExplanation: गैस के चूल्हे को सुविधाजनक मानते हुए पेड़ों की कटाई रोकने का संदेश दिया गया है। दूसरी पंक्ति वृक्षों को जीवंत प्रकृति का हिस्सा समझने को कहती है।
notes_20240423114641.context: Dated 2023-01-31 with “चूल्हा” as the prompt, the wording links gas stoves with reduced tree cutting. That environmental connection is the poem's own broad argument; no specific fuel policy or measured impact is identified.

literalEnglish: Once there was one shared stove; today there are four.
There is neither flavour in the food nor love in relationships.
notes_20240423114645.childFriendlyEnglish: Several separate kitchens become a picture of a family growing apart, with shared meals and affection both feeling diminished.
notes_20240423114645.simpleHindiExplanation: कभी संयुक्त परिवार में एक चूल्हा और साथ का भोजन था; अब अलग-अलग चूल्हे परिवार के बँटने का संकेत हैं। कवयित्री को भोजन के स्वाद के साथ रिश्तों का प्रेम भी घटता दिखता है।
notes_20240423114645.context: The note has no explicit date or मंच prompt in its raw text beyond the catalog's 2023-01-31 date and title “चूल्हा.” The shared-stove image appears to symbolize movement from a joint household to separate kitchens.

literalEnglish: As a kite tied to its string flies in the sky,
remain connected to family, bound by ties of love.
notes_20240423114649.childFriendlyEnglish: Like a kite that can soar because its string still holds it, people can grow while staying lovingly connected to family.
notes_20240423114649.simpleHindiExplanation: पतंग और धागे का रूपक बताता है कि ऊँचा उड़ते हुए भी परिवार से प्रेम का संबंध बना रहना चाहिए। जुड़ाव रोकता नहीं, सहारा देता है।
notes_20240423114649.context: Dated 2023-02-03 with “धागा” as the prompt, the poem uses a kite string as a metaphor for family bonds. It offers general advice rather than describing a specific family.

literalEnglish: The children are delighted because their favourite cartoon hero, Chhota Bheem, has arrived.
Munnu and Salim sit together to watch.
notes_20240423114652.childFriendlyEnglish: Two children happily watch Chhota Bheem together, showing how a favourite cartoon can bring friends into one shared moment.
notes_20240423114652.simpleHindiExplanation: मुन्नू और सलीम साथ बैठकर लोकप्रिय बाल-पात्र छोटा भीम देखते हैं। दोहे में बच्चों की खुशी और साथ देखने का सहज दृश्य है।
notes_20240423114652.context: The raw note gives 2023-02-03 and “भीम” as the prompt, while the catalog date is 2023-02-04. “छोटा भीम” clearly appears to name the animated children's character; Munnu and Salim are not otherwise identified.

literalEnglish: The British ruled India and lived in splendour.
They tied a knot of caste and religious division in people's minds.
notes_20240423114656.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem criticizes colonial rulers for enjoying power while deepening divisions of caste and religion among Indians.
notes_20240423114656.simpleHindiExplanation: अंग्रेजी शासन के वैभव और भारतीय समाज में जाति-धर्म के भेद बढ़ाने की नीति की आलोचना की गई है। गाँठ का रूपक मन में बैठी फूट को दिखाता है।
notes_20240423114656.context: Dated 2023-02-03 in the raw note and 2023-02-04 in the catalog, with “शासन” as the prompt, the verse invokes British colonial rule and a divide-and-rule interpretation. It does not cite a particular policy or incident.

literalEnglish: Independence has now reached the age of seventy-five years.
Through the government's good efforts, this period became known by the official phrase Amrit Kaal.
notes_20240423114700.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem marks seventy-five years of Indian independence and praises the government's vision of the period called Amrit Kaal.
notes_20240423114700.simpleHindiExplanation: भारत की आजादी के पचहत्तर वर्ष पूरे होने का उल्लेख है। कवयित्री शासन के प्रयासों की प्रशंसा करते हुए इस समय को प्रचलित सरकारी अभिव्यक्ति “अमृत काल” से जोड़ती हैं।
notes_20240423114700.context: The raw note is dated 2023-02-03 and prompted by “शासन,” while the catalog date is 2023-02-04. “Seventy-five years” and “Amrit Kaal” appear to refer to official language used around India's 75th anniversary of independence; the praise is the poem's viewpoint.

literalEnglish: One must certainly keep trying, even after falling repeatedly.
Victory comes to the person who never accepts defeat.
notes_20240423114703.childFriendlyEnglish: Falling many times does not end the journey; continuing to try without giving up can lead to success.
notes_20240423114703.simpleHindiExplanation: बार-बार असफल होने पर भी प्रयास जारी रखने की सीख है। जो व्यक्ति हार मानने से इनकार करता है, वही अंततः विजय पा सकता है।
notes_20240423114703.context: Dated 2023-02-04 with “अवश्य” as the prompt, the verse is a general statement about perseverance. It does not refer to a named competition, person, or event.

literalEnglish: Every line of the Manas is a vast storehouse of knowledge.
A person of limited understanding cannot grasp its essence.
notes_20240423114706.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem reveres the Ramcharitmanas as a deep book whose meaning requires patient and thoughtful reading.
notes_20240423114706.simpleHindiExplanation: मानस की पंक्तियों को विशाल ज्ञान-भंडार माना गया है। उसका सार समझने के लिए गहरी समझ और ध्यान से पढ़ना आवश्यक बताया गया है।
notes_20240423114706.context: Dated 2023-02-04 with “अल्प” as the prompt, “मानस” most likely refers to the Ramcharitmanas. The second line expresses the poem's evaluative devotional view, not a measured judgment of particular readers.

literalEnglish: Every line of the Manas is filled with profound knowledge.
Let the whole world read it; all its verse passages are true and worthy.
Knowledge is gained by the one who reads with understanding.
Shri Rama grants grace to the devotee who listens to it.
Respectfully submitted for review.
notes_20240423114713.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem invites people to read the Ramcharitmanas thoughtfully, saying that understanding its verses brings knowledge and listening with devotion brings Rama's blessing.
notes_20240423114713.simpleHindiExplanation: मानस की चौपाइयों को गहरे ज्ञान से भरा बताया गया है। केवल पढ़ना नहीं, समझकर पढ़ना जरूरी है; भक्तिभाव से सुनने वाले पर श्रीराम की कृपा होने का विश्वास भी व्यक्त है।
notes_20240423114713.context: The raw note is dated 2023-02-05 and labels the form as rola, while the catalog date is 2023-02-04. “मानस” and “श्री राम” make the Ramcharitmanas reference strong. “चौपाइयाँ” is retained as the name of its verse form.

literalEnglish: There is no other devotee like Hanuman, son of the wind.
Shri Rama dwells in his heart, making his life blessed.
notes_20240423114719.childFriendlyEnglish: Hanuman is praised as an unmatched devotee whose love for Rama fills his heart and gives his life sacred meaning.
notes_20240423114719.simpleHindiExplanation: पवनपुत्र हनुमान की राम-भक्ति को अनुपम बताया गया है। उनके हृदय में श्रीराम का निवास होने से उनका जीवन धन्य माना गया है।
notes_20240423114719.context: Dated 2023-02-06 with “अन्य” as the prompt, the verse uses familiar devotional names for Hanuman and Rama. It is a statement of faith, not a comparison based on historical evidence.

literalEnglish: Hunger / appetite
There is no life without water, and all the rivers are drying.
Farming too has become difficult; how will hunger be ended?
notes_20240423114723.childFriendlyEnglish: Drying rivers leave too little water for life and farming, so the poem asks how people will have enough food.
notes_20240423114723.simpleHindiExplanation: पानी की कमी और सूखती नदियों से जीवन तथा खेती दोनों संकट में पड़ते हैं। जब फसल उगाना कठिन होगा, तब भूख मिटाने की बड़ी समस्या खड़ी होगी।
notes_20240423114723.context: Dated 2023-02-06 with “भूख/क्षुधा” as the prompt, the poem directly connects water scarcity, drying rivers, difficult farming, and hunger. It names no particular drought, river, or region.

literalEnglish: Salutations to this country, which contains the four sacred dhams.
It has the twelve Jyotirlingas, and Shyam dwells in Vrindavan.
notes_20240423114729.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem bows to India by naming important Hindu pilgrimage traditions: the four dhams, twelve Jyotirlingas, and Krishna's Vrindavan.
notes_20240423114729.simpleHindiExplanation: भारत की पवित्र तीर्थ-परंपराओं को नमन किया गया है—चार धाम, बारह ज्योतिर्लिंग और वृंदावन में श्याम अर्थात कृष्ण की उपस्थिति।
notes_20240423114729.context: Dated 2023-02-06 with “नमो नमः” as the prompt, the verse gathers Hindu sacred geography into a patriotic-devotional salute. “Shyam” is interpreted as Krishna because Vrindavan is named.

literalEnglish: Giving notice of Phagun, palash flowers have begun to bloom.
Red silk-cotton blossoms have opened and seem to kiss the sky.
notes_20240423114741.childFriendlyEnglish: Bright palash and silk-cotton flowers announce the arrival of Phagun, filling the trees with red colour high against the sky.
notes_20240423114741.simpleHindiExplanation: पलाश और सेमल के लाल फूल फागुन आने की सूचना दे रहे हैं। ऊँचे खिले फूलों को आकाश चूमते हुए दिखाकर ऋतु का रंगीन दृश्य बनाया गया है।
notes_20240423114741.context: Dated 2023-02-08 with “सूचना” as the prompt, the poem uses palash and semal blossoms as seasonal signs of Phagun. It gives no specific location or botanical observation date beyond the preserved record.

literalEnglish: Topic: “Mischievous”
Competition number: 52
11 February 2023
Mischievous Krishna's exploits fill the heart with emotion.
Seeing his play, the gopis raise a commotion.
The gopis make a commotion when Krishna eats the butter.
They catch his hand and take him to Yashoda.
His mother grows angry and quickly ties Krishna up.
She raises a stick, and the mischievous child cries at the sight.
Respectfully submitted for review.
notes_20240423114826.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem retells a playful childhood scene in which Krishna steals butter, the gopis complain to Yashoda, and the usually mischievous child cries when his mother disciplines him.
notes_20240423114826.simpleHindiExplanation: बाल कृष्ण की माखन-चोरी की लीला का वर्णन है। गोपियाँ उन्हें पकड़कर यशोदा के पास ले जाती हैं; यशोदा बाँधती और छड़ी दिखाती हैं, तो नटखट कृष्ण रो पड़ते हैं।
notes_20240423114826.context: The record is cataloged as 2023-02-09 but preserves a competition ending date of 2023-02-11 and the topic “नटखट.” The narrative combines familiar Krishna childhood motifs of butter theft, complaints by gopis, and Yashoda binding him; exact details vary across devotional retellings.

literalEnglish: Political leaders make promises and appear trustworthy.
Once they gain power, they become intoxicated with it.
notes_20240423114831.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem warns that leaders may sound dependable while seeking votes but forget their promises after gaining power.
notes_20240423114831.simpleHindiExplanation: नेताओं के चुनावी या सार्वजनिक वादों पर व्यंग्य है। सत्ता मिलने से पहले वे भरोसेमंद बनते हैं, पर पद पाकर मद में वादे भूल सकते हैं।
notes_20240423114831.context: Dated 2023-02-09 with “विश्वस्त” as the prompt, the couplet offers general political satire about promises and power. No leader, party, election, or jurisdiction is identified.

literalEnglish: There is a heaven within India, and it is called Kashmir.
There lies the beautiful Dal Lake, filled with clear water.
notes_20240423114840.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem praises Kashmir's beauty by picturing clear water in Dal Lake and calling the region a heaven within India.
notes_20240423114840.simpleHindiExplanation: कश्मीर को भारत का स्वर्ग कहकर डल झील के सुंदर और निर्मल जल की प्रशंसा की गई है। यह प्राकृतिक सौंदर्य का काव्यात्मक वर्णन है।
notes_20240423114840.context: Dated 2023-02-09 with “झील” as the prompt, the verse explicitly names Kashmir and Dal Lake. Calling Kashmir “heaven” is poetic praise, not a literal geographic claim.

literalEnglish: Those who place duty above everything else,
such people earn respect in the world.
notes_20240423114843.childFriendlyEnglish: People who take their responsibilities seriously and put duty before convenience are likely to earn others' respect.
notes_20240423114843.simpleHindiExplanation: जो व्यक्ति अपने कर्तव्य को सबसे ऊपर रखता है और जिम्मेदारी निभाता है, उसे समाज में सम्मान मिलता है।
notes_20240423114843.context: Dated 2023-02-09 with “कर्तव्य” as the prompt, the poem gives a general ethical maxim. It does not define a particular duty or identify a profession or situation.

literalEnglish: Seeing Gajendra's faith, the Lord heard his call.
Taking the Sudarshan Chakra in hand, he killed the crocodile.
notes_20240423114847.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem recalls Gajendra calling to God when trapped by a crocodile and being rescued because of his faithful surrender.
notes_20240423114847.simpleHindiExplanation: गजेंद्र मोक्ष की पौराणिक कथा का संकेत है। ग्राह से संकट में पड़े गजेंद्र की आस्था और पुकार सुनकर भगवान सुदर्शन चक्र से उसकी रक्षा करते हैं।
notes_20240423114847.context: Dated 2023-02-10 with “आस्था” as the prompt, the verse clearly invokes the Gajendra Moksha episode. “ग्राह” denotes the crocodile-like attacker in the traditional narrative; the account is mythological and devotional.

literalEnglish: Tie a rope of love so that the family remains united.
Seeing everyone together, an enemy will not attack.
notes_20240423114851.childFriendlyEnglish: Love is imagined as a rope that keeps a family together, and unity gives its members greater strength and safety.
notes_20240423114851.simpleHindiExplanation: प्रेम की रस्सी परिवार को जोड़े रखने का रूपक है। सबके साथ रहने से परिवार मजबूत दिखता है और विरोधी भी नुकसान पहुँचाने से हिचकता है।
notes_20240423114851.context: Dated 2023-02-10 with “रस्सी” as the prompt, the first line is clearly metaphorical. “Enemy” is left general because the poem names no person, conflict, or literal threat.

literalEnglish: Filled with faith, Draupadi kept calling to the Lord.
Krishna lengthened her garment, astonishing the royal court.
notes_20240423114854.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem recalls Draupadi praying during her humiliation and Krishna protecting her before the shocked royal assembly.
notes_20240423114854.simpleHindiExplanation: महाभारत के चीरहरण प्रसंग में द्रौपदी की आस्था और पुकार का वर्णन है। कृष्ण उनके वस्त्र को बढ़ाकर भरी सभा में उनकी रक्षा करते हैं।
notes_20240423114854.context: Dated 2023-02-10 with “आस्था” as the prompt, the verse invokes the Mahabharata disrobing episode and a devotional tradition in which Krishna miraculously protects Draupadi. It should be read as sacred narrative, not independently verified history.

literalEnglish: The Ganga can be found even in a small basin, says Saint Ravidas.
Through faith and trust, the Lord remains near.
notes_20240423114858.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem says that a sincere and faithful heart can find holiness even in an ordinary bowl, without needing outward grandeur.
notes_20240423114858.simpleHindiExplanation: संत रविदास से जुड़ी प्रसिद्ध उक्ति “मन चंगा तो कठौती में गंगा” का भाव है। सच्ची आस्था और विश्वास से साधारण स्थान में भी ईश्वर की निकटता अनुभव की जा सकती है।
notes_20240423114858.context: Dated 2023-02-10 with “आस्था” as the prompt, the verse appears to echo the saying popularly associated with Ravidas about finding the Ganga in a kathauti when the mind is pure. The exact historical wording or attribution is not established here.

literalEnglish: Prayag, king of confluences, is the meeting place of faith and trust.
Take a dip in the name of Hari, and one's fortune awakens.
notes_20240423114903.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem joins Prayag's sacred confluence with an inward immersion in God's name, suggesting that devotion can renew hope and blessing.
notes_20240423114903.simpleHindiExplanation: प्रयाग के संगम को आस्था और विश्वास का मिलन कहा गया है। हरि-नाम में डुबकी लगाने का अर्थ केवल जल-स्नान नहीं, बल्कि भक्तिभाव में डूबना भी हो सकता है।
notes_20240423114903.context: Dated 2023-02-10 with “आस्था” as the prompt, the poem names Prayag as “संगम राज” and pairs pilgrimage imagery with Hari devotion. Whether “डुबकी” is meant literally, metaphorically, or both is ambiguous.

literalEnglish: Those who carry daggers in their hands treat life as a game.
Beware of such people; do not associate with them.
notes_20240423114907.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem advises staying away from people who carry weapons and show no respect for the value of life.
notes_20240423114907.simpleHindiExplanation: हथियार लेकर जीवन को खेल समझने वाले हिंसक लोगों से सावधान रहने और उनसे मेल-जोल न रखने की सलाह दी गई है।
notes_20240423114907.context: The catalog date is 2023-02-11, while the raw note gives 2023-02-10 and “खंजर” as the prompt. The warning is general; no crime, group, or incident is identified.

literalEnglish: Wounds made by a dagger have a treatment.
Wounds made by words do not heal, however much one tries.
notes_20240423114915.childFriendlyEnglish: Physical cuts may receive medicine, but cruel words can leave emotional pain that lasts much longer.
notes_20240423114915.simpleHindiExplanation: खंजर के शारीरिक घाव का इलाज हो सकता है, पर कटु शब्द मन पर गहरी चोट करते हैं और उनका भरना बहुत कठिन होता है।
notes_20240423114915.context: Dated 2023-02-11 with “खंजर” as the prompt, the poem contrasts literal injury with the metaphorical wounds caused by speech. The absolute phrasing is poetic emphasis, not a medical claim.

literalEnglish: The eyes themselves have become deadly; what need is there for a dagger?
Whoever they looked upon lovingly was completely overcome.
notes_20240423114919.childFriendlyEnglish: In playful romantic exaggeration, a loving glance is described as more powerful than a dagger because it leaves the beloved helplessly enchanted.
notes_20240423114919.simpleHindiExplanation: प्रेमपूर्ण आँखों को खंजर से भी अधिक असरदार बताने वाला हास्यपूर्ण शृंगारिक अतिशयोक्ति है। “काम तमाम” यहाँ सचमुच मृत्यु नहीं, प्रेम में घायल या मोहित होने का संकेत लगता है।
notes_20240423114919.context: Dated 2023-02-11 with “खंजर” as the prompt, the couplet uses conventional romantic hyperbole about killing glances. The phrase “काम तमाम” is interpreted figuratively because the second line explicitly says the look is loving.

literalEnglish: If you seek the path to liberation, chant Rama's name.
Through his sacred name, every task finds completion.
notes_20240423114925.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem presents remembrance of Rama as a spiritual path that gives believers hope, direction, and confidence in life's work.
notes_20240423114925.simpleHindiExplanation: मुक्ति पाने के लिए राम-नाम भजने की सीख दी गई है। उनके पवित्र नाम को जीवन के काम सँवारने और आध्यात्मिक मार्ग दिखाने वाला माना गया है।
notes_20240423114925.context: Dated 2023-02-11 with “मार्ग” as the prompt, the verse expresses a devotional belief in the power of Rama's name. “All tasks” is faith language and should not be read as a guaranteed practical outcome.

literalEnglish: Filled with devotion, Draupadi kept calling to the Lord.
Krishna lengthened her garment, astonishing the royal court.
The royal court was astonished as Dushasana grew exhausted.
Krishna did not tolerate Krishnaa's humiliation.
In the full assembly, he protected his friend's honour.
Everyone was amazed, and their devotion to the Lord increased.
notes_20240423114929.childFriendlyEnglish: This longer retelling shows Draupadi calling for help, Dushasana failing to strip her, and Krishna preserving her dignity before the astonished court.
notes_20240423114929.simpleHindiExplanation: कुंडलिया में द्रौपदी-चीरहरण प्रसंग का विस्तार है। द्रौपदी की पुकार पर कृष्ण वस्त्र बढ़ाते हैं, दुःशासन हारता है और सभा में उनकी प्रतिष्ठा बचती है; इसे प्रभु-निष्ठा बढ़ाने वाली घटना माना गया है।
notes_20240423114929.context: Dated 2023-02-11 and titled only “कुंडलिया,” the poem invokes the Mahabharata episode of Draupadi's attempted disrobing. “कृष्णा” is another name for Draupadi here, while “कृष्ण” names the deity; “सखी” conveys a devotional friendship relationship.

literalEnglish: New units of measurement came into use, and the gaz was forgotten.
Only a few people like us remain exceptions here.
notes_20240423114933.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem notices that modern measurement units have replaced the old gaz, though some older people still remember and use it.
notes_20240423114933.simpleHindiExplanation: नई माप-प्रणालियों के आने से पुरानी इकाई “गज” का प्रयोग घट गया है। कवयित्री अपने जैसे कुछ लोगों को उसका अपवाद बताती हैं, जो अभी उसे याद रखते हैं।
notes_20240423114933.context: Dated 2023-02-12 with “गज” as the prompt, the verse uses “गज” as the traditional unit of length, not as an elephant. The identity or age of the remaining users is not specified.

literalEnglish: Only two gaz of earth are finally needed, yet people do not understand.
In the end, hoarded wealth is of no use.
notes_20240423114937.childFriendlyEnglish: Because every life ends with only a small resting place, the poem asks why people spend their lives endlessly collecting wealth.
notes_20240423114937.simpleHindiExplanation: मनुष्य के अंतिम संस्कार या कब्र के लिए थोड़ी-सी धरती पर्याप्त होने के रूपक से धन-संचय की निरर्थकता बताई गई है। मृत्यु के बाद जमा संपत्ति साथ नहीं जाती।
notes_20240423114937.context: Dated 2023-02-12 with “गज” as the prompt, “दो गज धरती” is a familiar expression for the small amount of ground associated with death or burial. The verse is a moral reflection, not a precise description of funeral requirements.

literalEnglish: A lion on its own should not attack an elephant.
The elephant has greater strength, and the lion is defeated.
notes_20240423114942.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem advises against attacking a stronger opponent alone, using a lion and an elephant to show the need to judge strength wisely.
notes_20240423114942.simpleHindiExplanation: अकेले सिंह और शक्तिशाली हाथी की तुलना से समझदारी की सीख दी गई है कि बिना अपनी और सामने वाले की ताकत आँके आक्रमण नहीं करना चाहिए।
notes_20240423114942.context: Dated 2023-02-12 with “गज” as the prompt, “गज” means elephant here. The animal outcome is presented as a poetic lesson; it is not a scientific claim that every elephant defeats every lion.

literalEnglish: When the ocean was churned, many treasures emerged.
Indra's elephant Airavata was one of them.
notes_20240423114946.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem recalls the mythic churning of the ocean, when many wondrous treasures appeared, including Indra's elephant Airavata.
notes_20240423114946.simpleHindiExplanation: समुद्र-मंथन की पौराणिक कथा में निकले अनेक रत्नों में इंद्र के हाथी ऐरावत को भी एक बताया गया है। यहाँ “गज” का अर्थ हाथी है।
notes_20240423114946.context: Dated 2023-02-12 with “गज” as the prompt, the verse clearly refers to the Hindu Samudra Manthan narrative and Airavata's association with Indra. This is mythological context, not historical reporting.

literalEnglish: Do not be so doubtful about a text such as the Manas.
Read the episode carefully; there is no casteism in it.
notes_20240423114952.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem asks readers not to judge the Ramcharitmanas too quickly and says disputed passages should be read closely and in context.
notes_20240423114952.simpleHindiExplanation: मानस पर संदेह करने के बजाय संबंधित प्रसंग को ध्यान से पढ़ने की सलाह दी गई है। जातिवाद न होने का निष्कर्ष कवयित्री का मत है; बहस का कौन-सा प्रसंग है, यह दोहे में स्पष्ट नहीं।
notes_20240423114952.context: Dated 2023-02-12 with “सशंकित” as the prompt, “मानस” likely means the Ramcharitmanas. The wording appears to respond to a caste-related criticism or controversy, but no passage, critic, or contemporary event is named, so the specific trigger is uncertain.

literalEnglish: Understand the purpose of life, my friend.
Always moving forward is the way of this life.
notes_20240423114957.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem encourages a friend to find direction in life and keep making progress rather than remaining stuck.
notes_20240423114957.simpleHindiExplanation: जीवन का उद्देश्य समझकर निरंतर आगे बढ़ने की प्रेरणा दी गई है। रुकने के बजाय सीखते और प्रगति करते रहना जीवन की रीति बताई गई है।
notes_20240423114957.context: The catalog date is 2023-02-12, while the raw note gives 2023-02-13 and “उद्देश्य” as the prompt. The advice is general and does not define one universal purpose beyond continued progress.

literalEnglish: The full flourishing of Phagun is now visible upon the earth.
Nature's adornment has spread joy throughout the world.
notes_20240423115001.childFriendlyEnglish: Phagun's flowers and fresh beauty make the earth look richly decorated and fill people with seasonal joy.
notes_20240423115001.simpleHindiExplanation: फागुन में प्रकृति का पूरा सौंदर्य धरती पर दिखाई देता है। उसके रंग और श्रृंगार से चारों ओर प्रसन्नता फैलती है।
notes_20240423115001.context: Dated 2023-02-13 with “उत्कर्ष” as the prompt, the poem applies the word to the peak beauty of Phagun. No particular landscape or celebration is identified.

literalEnglish: The country's economy is number five in the world.
This, truly, is evidence of India's rise.
notes_20240423115006.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem celebrates reports that India's economy had become the world's fifth largest and treats that ranking as a sign of national progress.
notes_20240423115006.simpleHindiExplanation: भारत की अर्थव्यवस्था को विश्व में पाँचवें स्थान पर बताकर इसे देश के उत्कर्ष और प्रगति का प्रमाण माना गया है। यह रैंकिंग पर आधारित गर्व का भाव है।
notes_20240423115006.context: Dated 2023-02-13 with “उत्कर्ष” as the prompt, the verse appears to refer to widely reported nominal-GDP rankings in which India was described as the fifth-largest economy. It does not name the dataset, year of comparison, or economic measure, so the claim should remain qualified.

literalEnglish: Number: 02
The sky began to fall, and the ground began to fly.
Believe it only when you have seen it with your own eyes.
notes_20240423115010.childFriendlyEnglish: By describing impossible things, the poem humorously advises people not to believe extraordinary claims without seeing reliable evidence.
notes_20240423115010.simpleHindiExplanation: आसमान गिरने और जमीन उड़ने जैसी असंभव बातों से अतिशयोक्ति रची गई है। संदेश है कि विचित्र दावों पर तुरंत विश्वास न करें और प्रमाण देखकर ही यकीन करें।
notes_20240423115010.context: The record is dated 2023-02-13 and labels itself as completion line number 02, but no separate prompt line survives in the parsed text. The first poetic line is deliberately impossible; the precise source or rules of the line-completion exercise are not preserved here.

literalEnglish: Human life is formed like a heap of sand.
When the wind blows, it collapses without taking any time.
notes_20240423115014.childFriendlyEnglish: A sand pile can fall apart in a moment, and the poem uses it to remind us that human life is fragile and uncertain.
notes_20240423115014.simpleHindiExplanation: मानव जीवन की नश्वरता को बालू के ढेर से तुलना करके दिखाया गया है। जैसे हवा से रेत तुरंत बिखर सकती है, वैसे ही जीवन भी अस्थिर है।
notes_20240423115014.context: The catalog date is 2023-02-13, while the raw metadata gives 2023-02-03 and “रेत/बालू” as the prompt. The sand heap is a metaphor for mortality and fragility; the date discrepancy is unresolved.

literalEnglish: A flight campaign has begun in Bengaluru.
New trainees now fly in aircraft,
like the flying monkey-god Hanuman.
notes_20240423115024.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem links an aviation-training initiative in Bengaluru with Hanuman's famous flight, celebrating new trainees taking to the air.
notes_20240423115024.simpleHindiExplanation: बेंगलुरु में शुरू किसी उड़ान या विमान-प्रशिक्षण अभियान का उल्लेख है। नए प्रशिक्षुओं की उड़ान की तुलना पौराणिक हनुमान की आकाश-यात्रा से की गई है।
notes_20240423115024.context: The catalog date is 2023-02-13, while the raw note gives 2023-02-14 and “उड़ान” as the prompt. The wording may refer to an aviation training campaign or event in Bengaluru, but no program name or organization is given; the exact reference remains uncertain.

literalEnglish: The young bride goes to her beloved's home, carrying a tender heart.
Beloved, do not leave her side; keep holding her hand.
notes_20240423115031.childFriendlyEnglish: As a bride enters a new home with a sensitive heart, the poem asks her partner to stay close, support her, and not let her feel alone.
notes_20240423115031.simpleHindiExplanation: नववधू कोमल मन लेकर पति के घर जा रही है। प्रियतम से कहा गया है कि उसका साथ न छोड़े और हाथ थामकर भावनात्मक सहारा दे।
notes_20240423115031.context: Dated 2023-02-14 with “कोमल/नाजुक” as the prompt, the verse uses traditional bridal language. It does not identify a real couple or specify whether it was written for a particular wedding.

literalEnglish: Everyone is amazed on seeing the baya weaverbird's nest.
Nature gave it skill and remarkable knowledge.
notes_20240423115035.childFriendlyEnglish: The carefully woven nest of the baya bird inspires wonder at the building ability that comes naturally to it.
notes_20240423115035.simpleHindiExplanation: बया पक्षी के जटिल और सुंदर घोंसले को देखकर लोग चकित होते हैं। उसकी स्वाभाविक निर्माण-कुशलता को प्रकृति का अद्भुत उपहार कहा गया है।
notes_20240423115035.context: Dated 2023-02-14 with “कौशल” as the prompt, the poem refers to the baya weaverbird's distinctive woven nest. “Knowledge” is poetic personification of instinctive or learned bird behaviour, not a technical biological explanation.

literalEnglish: Phagun has arrived, friend, and the earth adorns herself.
Dressed in silk-cotton and palash blossoms, she looks like a married woman.
notes_20240423115040.childFriendlyEnglish: Red semal and palash flowers dress the earth for Phagun as beautifully as a bride wearing festive adornments.
notes_20240423115040.simpleHindiExplanation: फागुन में सेमल और टेसू के लाल फूलों से सजी धरती का मानवीकरण किया गया है। उसे श्रृंगार की हुई सुहागिन स्त्री जैसा सुंदर बताया गया है।
