notes_20240423123200.context: The record is dated 2023-06-07 and uses “भ्राता” as the prompt. The Ravana reference appears to draw a moral lesson from the Ramayana, though the particular fraternal injustice intended is not named.

literalEnglish: Lord Jagannath’s flag flies against the wind.
It has become a wondrous riddle—can you solve it, friend?
notes_20240423123204.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem shares a popular wonder associated with Jagannath Temple: its flag seems to fly in an unexpected direction, inviting the reader to puzzle over it.
notes_20240423123204.simpleHindiExplanation: दोहा जगन्नाथ मंदिर की ध्वजा के हवा के विपरीत उड़ने की प्रचलित धारणा को पहेली की तरह प्रस्तुत करता है। यह पंक्तियाँ धार्मिक आश्चर्य व्यक्त करती हैं, वैज्ञानिक प्रमाण नहीं।
notes_20240423123204.context: The record is dated 2023-06-07 and names “पहेली” as the prompt. It repeats a popular claim about the flag at Jagannath Temple; the verse itself does not provide evidence or an explanation for that claim.

literalEnglish: For reasons that were merely alleged, Sita was sent into exile.
Though she had undergone the trial by fire, her suffering still did not end.
notes_20240423123207.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem feels sorrow for Sita, who continued to suffer even after she had already faced a severe test. It questions the fairness of judging her again.
notes_20240423123207.simpleHindiExplanation: सीता की अग्नि-परीक्षा के बाद भी उन्हें वनवास मिलने की पीड़ा और अन्याय पर दोहा ध्यान देता है। “कथित कारण” समाज के आरोपों या धारणाओं पर प्रश्न उठाता है।
notes_20240423123207.context: The preserved record is dated 2023-06-08 and gives “कथित” as the prompt. It appears to refer to the later exile of Sita in Ramayana tradition and adopts a critical, sympathetic tone toward her ordeal.

literalEnglish: Read the Ramayana and Gita, and keep your thoughts pure.
When thoughts are pure, corrupt impulses do not arise.
notes_20240423123210.childFriendlyEnglish: Reading teachings that encourage goodness can help us think carefully and avoid harmful habits, according to the poem.
notes_20240423123210.simpleHindiExplanation: रामायण और गीता के अध्ययन से विचारों को शुद्ध रखने की प्रेरणा दी गई है। दोहा मानता है कि अच्छे विचार मन के विकारों को दूर रखने में सहायक होते हैं।
notes_20240423123210.context: The record is dated 2023-06-08 and names “विकार” as the prompt. It presents a devotional-moral belief about scripture and thought, not a clinical claim about mental health.

literalEnglish: To determine direction, make use of a magnet.
People carry it among mountains, seas, and distant horizons.
notes_20240423123213.childFriendlyEnglish: A magnetic compass helps travellers find direction in places where the route is hard to see, such as mountains or the open sea.
notes_20240423123213.simpleHindiExplanation: दिशा जानने के लिए चुंबक या चुंबकीय कंपास के उपयोग की बात कही गई है। पर्वत और समुद्र जैसी जगहों में यह यात्रियों के मार्गदर्शन का साधन बनता है।
notes_20240423123213.context: The preserved date is 2023-06-08, while the internal मंच date is 2023-06-09, and the prompt is “चुंबक.” “क्षितिज” makes the second line somewhat compressed, but the central reference is to magnetic navigation.

literalEnglish: Doha: 9 June 2023
Ink and paper have fallen behind as smartphones advance.
A shorter route has been found for reading and writing.
notes_20240423123216.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem notices how smartphones make reading and writing quicker, while traditional ink and paper are used less often.
notes_20240423123216.simpleHindiExplanation: स्मार्टफोन के बढ़ते उपयोग से स्याही और कागज पीछे छूटते दिख रहे हैं। पढ़ने-लिखने का रास्ता छोटा और तेज हुआ है, यद्यपि दोहा इसके लाभ-हानि का पूरा निर्णय नहीं देता।
notes_20240423123216.context: The preserved record is dated 2023-06-09 and includes “कागज” as a heading rather than a clearly marked provided prompt. The opening date line is retained because it is present in the parsed body.

literalEnglish: If you are hungry and cannot find any grain,
you remain destitute even with diamonds and pearls in your pocket.
notes_20240423123220.childFriendlyEnglish: Food matters more than jewels when someone is hungry. Wealth is not truly useful if it cannot provide a basic need.
notes_20240423123220.simpleHindiExplanation: भूख के समय अन्न न मिले तो हीरे-मोती भी बेकार हो जाते हैं। दोहा जीवन की मूल आवश्यकता के सामने धन और आभूषण की सीमित उपयोगिता दिखाता है।
notes_20240423123220.context: The record is dated 2023-06-11 and names “अन्न” as the prompt. It contrasts food with luxury objects to make a general point about basic needs.

literalEnglish: One who can satisfy hunger is called prosperous.
A hungry person needs only two handfuls of grain.
notes_20240423123223.childFriendlyEnglish: Real abundance means having enough food and being able to feed someone who is hungry, not simply owning expensive things.
notes_20240423123223.simpleHindiExplanation: सच्ची संपन्नता वह है जो भूख मिटा सके। भूखे व्यक्ति के लिए थोड़े से अन्न का मूल्य बड़े धन से भी अधिक होता है।
notes_20240423123223.context: The preserved record is dated 2023-06-11 and gives “अन्न” as the prompt. The poem defines prosperity through the ability to meet hunger, using “two handfuls” figuratively for a modest meal.

literalEnglish: After hoarding high-denomination notes, people were left helpless.
The vast stockpile they had filled became useless.
notes_20240423123228.childFriendlyEnglish: Money secretly stored in large notes can suddenly lose its usefulness. The poem warns that merely piling up cash does not guarantee security.
notes_20240423123228.simpleHindiExplanation: बड़े नोट जमा करने वालों के अचानक लाचार होने और उनका विशाल भंडार बेकार पड़ने का चित्र है। यह संभवतः नोटबंदी की स्मृति की ओर संकेत करता है, पर घटना स्पष्ट रूप से नहीं लिखी गई।
notes_20240423123228.context: The record is dated 2023-06-11 and has “वृहद” as a heading, without a clearly marked prompt. The wording appears to recall the invalidation of high-denomination currency, possibly India’s 2016 demonetisation, but that event is not named, so the identification remains tentative.

literalEnglish: When hunger strikes and no food grain can be found,
even with diamonds and pearls in your pocket, you are still in need.
notes_20240423123232.childFriendlyEnglish: A hungry person needs food, not precious stones. This version again stresses that basic necessities are a more meaningful kind of wealth.
notes_20240423123232.simpleHindiExplanation: यह समान पंक्तियों वाला अलग संरक्षित अभिलेख है। इसमें फिर कहा गया है कि भूख के समय अन्न न हो तो जेब के हीरे-मोती भी मनुष्य की विपन्नता दूर नहीं कर सकते।
notes_20240423123232.context: This separate preserved record is dated 2023-06-11 and again names “अन्न” as the prompt. Its verse text matches the earlier record notes_20240423123220, so no distinct occasion or intention is inferred.

literalEnglish: Sachin struck a century, leaving Shane Warne astonished.
He played a blazing innings, making India proud.
notes_20240423123236.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem celebrates a powerful Sachin Tendulkar innings against bowler Shane Warne and the pride it brought Indian cricket fans.
notes_20240423123236.simpleHindiExplanation: सचिन तेंदुलकर के शतक और आक्रामक पारी का उत्सव मनाया गया है। शेन वॉर्न का नाम इस प्रदर्शन के सामने चकित प्रतिद्वंद्वी के रूप में आता है।
notes_20240423123236.context: The record is dated 2023-06-12 and names “शतक” as the prompt. It evokes Sachin Tendulkar’s famous contests with Shane Warne, but the wording does not identify one particular match or innings.

literalEnglish: By circling his mother, he earned the right to be worshipped first.
Revered Ganesha travels seated upon his mouse vehicle.
notes_20240423123311.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem recalls Ganesha honouring his parents as his whole world and becoming the deity worshipped first. It also pictures him riding his tiny mouse.
notes_20240423123311.simpleHindiExplanation: गणेश जी द्वारा माता की प्रदक्षिणा करके प्रथम पूज्य बनने की पौराणिक कथा का संकेत है। दूसरी पंक्ति उनके मूषक वाहन का वर्णन करती है।
notes_20240423123311.context: The preserved record is dated 2023-06-12 and names “वाहन” as the prompt. It appears to compress the familiar story of Ganesha circling his parents and receiving precedence in worship; the line specifically says “mother.”

literalEnglish: The mighty thunderbolt was made from sage Dadhichi’s bones.
It belongs to Lord Indra—behold his splendour.
notes_20240423123316.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem recalls the myth in which sage Dadhichi gives his bones so Indra can receive the powerful vajra, highlighting sacrifice and divine strength.
notes_20240423123316.simpleHindiExplanation: ऋषि दधीचि की अस्थियों से इंद्र का वज्र बनने की पौराणिक कथा कही गई है। इसमें दधीचि के त्याग और इंद्र के शक्तिशाली अस्त्र दोनों का स्मरण है।
notes_20240423123316.context: The record is dated 2023-06-13 and gives “वज्र” as the prompt. It directly invokes the Hindu myth of Dadhichi’s self-sacrifice and Indra’s thunderbolt.

literalEnglish: After asking for a boon, Kumbhakarna sleeps for six months.
He said “Nidrasana,” though he had hoped for “Indrasana.”
notes_20240423123321.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem retells a playful myth about Kumbhakarna’s words being changed: instead of asking for Indra’s throne, he ends up asking for deep sleep.
notes_20240423123321.simpleHindiExplanation: कुंभकर्ण के वरदान से जुड़ी प्रचलित कथा का संकेत है। वह इंद्रासन माँगना चाहता था, पर “निद्रासन” कहने से उसे लंबे समय तक सोने का वर मिला—कथा के रूप अलग-अलग मिलते हैं।
notes_20240423123321.context: The preserved record is dated 2023-06-13 and names “शयन” as the prompt. It uses a popular Ramayana-related wordplay about Kumbhakarna requesting “Nidrasana” instead of “Indrasana”; versions of this legend vary.

literalEnglish: Rama lifted the bow, and it broke at once.
King Janaka’s sadness cleared, and Sita rejoiced.
notes_20240423123324.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem recalls Rama lifting and breaking Shiva’s bow, fulfilling the challenge that allows Sita’s marriage and bringing relief to her father Janaka.
notes_20240423123324.simpleHindiExplanation: सीता स्वयंवर में राम द्वारा धनुष उठाकर तोड़ने का प्रसंग है। इससे राजा जनक की उदासी दूर होती है और सीता प्रसन्न होती हैं।
notes_20240423123324.context: The record is dated 2023-06-14 and names “उदासी” as the prompt. The bow, Janaka, and Sita clearly point to the bow-breaking episode in Ramayana tradition.

literalEnglish: Lakshmana left his bed and gave up sleep.
Devoted to serving the Lord, he stayed awake and watchful.
notes_20240423123329.childFriendlyEnglish: Lakshmana’s wakefulness shows his dedication to Rama. He gives up comfort so he can remain alert and serve during their journey.
notes_20240423123329.simpleHindiExplanation: लक्ष्मण ने शैया और नींद त्यागकर राम की सेवा में सतर्क रहने का संकल्प निभाया। दोहा उनके त्याग, सेवा और चौकसी को रेखांकित करता है।
notes_20240423123329.context: The preserved record is dated 2023-06-14 and gives “शैया” as the prompt. It refers to Lakshmana’s devoted service to Rama during the Ramayana exile.

literalEnglish: Do not create an uproar; accept this argument.
When the country is undivided, let its law be uniform.
notes_20240423123350.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem argues that one united country should follow the same law everywhere and asks people to discuss the idea without creating disorder.
notes_20240423123350.simpleHindiExplanation: दोहा हंगामा न करने और अखंड देश में समान कानून स्वीकार करने की बात कहता है। यह कवयित्री का राजनीतिक-नागरिक मत है; किसी विशेष विधेयक का नाम नहीं दिया गया।
notes_20240423123350.context: The record is dated 2023-06-15 and names “हंगामा” as the prompt. Its wording appears to support a uniform legal framework for the country, possibly the public idea of a Uniform Civil Code, but no policy is explicitly named.

literalEnglish: By keeping dependants in the country, the country now regrets it.
Whichever tree the dodder vine climbs, it consumes that tree.
notes_20240423123355.childFriendlyEnglish: Using a parasitic vine as an image, the poem warns that unhealthy dependence can weaken the very source that supports it. It does not say exactly whom the comparison describes.
notes_20240423123355.simpleHindiExplanation: अमरबेल के रूपक से ऐसी निर्भरता की आलोचना की गई है जो सहारा देने वाले को ही नुकसान पहुँचाए। पहली पंक्ति में “आश्रित” किस व्यक्ति या समूह के लिए है, यह स्पष्ट नहीं है।
notes_20240423123355.context: The preserved record is dated 2023-06-15 and names “आश्रित” as the prompt. The country-and-dodder comparison has political or social overtones, but the target is unstated and should not be inferred.

literalEnglish: Those dependent on a banyan tree never become trees themselves.
They always remain green, yet only at the level of grass.
notes_20240423123400.childFriendlyEnglish: Constantly relying on a powerful protector may keep someone comfortable but can prevent independent growth. The plant image encourages standing on one’s own.
notes_20240423123400.simpleHindiExplanation: बरगद पर आश्रित हरियाली के रूपक से बताया गया है कि केवल सहारे पर रहने से अपना बड़ा विकास नहीं हो पाता। जीववैज्ञानिक विवरण से अधिक यह आत्मनिर्भरता की नैतिक उपमा है।
notes_20240423123400.context: The record is dated 2023-06-15 and gives “आश्रित” as the prompt. The botanical image is somewhat imprecise, but it appears to function as a metaphor for dependence limiting growth.

literalEnglish: The clever cuckoo leaves its dependent eggs in another’s care.
The crow raises them, receiving no gratitude.
notes_20240423123403.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem describes the cuckoo laying eggs for a crow to raise. It treats this natural behaviour as a witty lesson about receiving help without thanks.
notes_20240423123403.simpleHindiExplanation: कोयल के अंडे कौवे के घोंसले में पलने की प्राकृतिक घटना को दोहे ने मानवीय चतुराई और एहसान न मानने के रूपक में बदला है। यह पक्षियों के व्यवहार का नैतिकीकृत चित्रण है।
notes_20240423123403.context: The preserved record is dated 2023-06-15 and names “आश्रित” as the prompt. It refers to brood parasitism by cuckoos, while assigning human ideas such as cleverness and gratitude for poetic effect.

literalEnglish: Doha: 15 June 2023
One country always has one system of law.
When the country is undivided, let the law be uniform.
notes_20240423123407.childFriendlyEnglish: This poem repeats the view that a united nation should have a common legal system for all its people.
notes_20240423123407.simpleHindiExplanation: अखंड देश के लिए एक समान विधान और कानून की वकालत की गई है। यह एक राजनीतिक-नागरिक विचार है, पर पंक्तियाँ किसी खास कानून या समुदाय का उल्लेख नहीं करतीं।
notes_20240423123407.context: The preserved record is dated 2023-06-15 and has “कानून” as a heading rather than a clearly marked provided prompt. It may relate to debate about a Uniform Civil Code, but the verse only states a general one-country, one-law position. The opening date line is retained from the parsed body.

literalEnglish: All the politicians have gathered, forgetting civility.
To gain power, they are searching for a strategy.
notes_20240423123411.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem criticizes politicians who set good manners aside and focus on clever ways to win power.
notes_20240423123411.simpleHindiExplanation: सत्ता पाने के लिए जुटे नेताओं पर व्यंग्य है, जो तहज़ीब भूलकर केवल तरकीब खोज रहे हैं। किसी दल, गठबंधन या चुनाव का नाम नहीं दिया गया।
notes_20240423123411.context: The record is dated 2023-06-16 and identifies “तरकीब” as the prompt. It is a general political satire; the wording does not support tying it to a particular party or event.

literalEnglish: Taking the inexhaustible quiver and the Gandiva bow with him,
Partha laid the foundation of victory at Kurukshetra.
notes_20240423123414.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem pictures Arjuna entering the Kurukshetra war equipped with his famous Gandiva bow and an unfailing supply of arrows.
notes_20240423123414.simpleHindiExplanation: महाभारत के अर्जुन—पार्थ—का चित्र है, जो गांडीव धनुष और अक्षय तरकश लेकर कुरुक्षेत्र में युद्ध करते हैं। इन्हीं साधनों से विजय की नींव रखने की बात कही गई है।
notes_20240423123414.context: The preserved date is 2023-06-16, while the internal मंच date is 2023-06-17, and the prompt is “तरकश.” “Partha,” Gandiva, and Kurukshetra identify Arjuna and the Mahabharata war.

literalEnglish: Now everyone lives in flats and is not fortunate enough to have a rooftop.
There is no longer a way to enjoy the courtyard’s comforting shade.
notes_20240423123418.childFriendlyEnglish: Modern flats can save space, but the poem misses the open rooftop, courtyard, and shade that older homes offered families.
notes_20240423123418.simpleHindiExplanation: फ्लैटों में रहने के कारण निजी छत और आँगन की खुली छाया का सुख कम हो गया है। दोहा आधुनिक आवास के साथ खोती घरेलू जगहों के प्रति स्मृति और कमी व्यक्त करता है।
notes_20240423123418.context: The record is dated 2023-06-17 and names “छत” as the prompt. It contrasts apartment living with traditional homes that had accessible rooftops and courtyards.

literalEnglish: The terror of COVID left the world stunned.
Countless lives were lost, and innumerable people were left destitute.
notes_20240423123421.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem remembers the fear, deaths, and financial hardship caused around the world by the COVID-19 pandemic.
notes_20240423123421.simpleHindiExplanation: कोविड महामारी से विश्व के स्तब्ध होने, बहुत-सी जानें जाने और असंख्य लोगों के आर्थिक संकट में पड़ने का स्मरण है।
notes_20240423123421.context: The preserved date is 2023-06-17, while the internal मंच date is 2023-06-18, and the prompt is “सन्न.” The reference to COVID and its human and economic losses is explicit.

literalEnglish: The sunlight at sunrise brings relief from illnesses.
It provides several nutrients, with vitamin D foremost among them.
notes_20240423123424.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem encourages enjoying morning sunlight and connects it with vitamin D. Its broad promise of curing illness should be read as poetic health advice, not medical guidance.
notes_20240423123424.simpleHindiExplanation: सुबह की धूप को स्वास्थ्य और विटामिन डी से जोड़ा गया है। “रोग निदान” का दावा बहुत व्यापक है; धूप चिकित्सा का विकल्प नहीं और अधिक धूप से बचाव भी आवश्यक है।
notes_20240423123424.context: The record is dated 2023-06-19 and uses “सूर्योदय” as a heading without a clearly marked prompt. Sun exposure can support vitamin D production, but sunlight does not diagnose or cure diseases as broadly as the poetic wording suggests.

literalEnglish: Rise before sunrise and practise yoga.
Doctors, medicines, and illnesses will stay far from you.
notes_20240423123428.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem recommends an early routine and yoga for good health. Exercise can help well-being, though it cannot guarantee that a person will never need medicine or a doctor.
notes_20240423123428.simpleHindiExplanation: सूर्योदय से पहले उठकर योग करने की स्वास्थ्यकर दिनचर्या सुझाई गई है। डॉक्टर, औषधि और रोग से पूरी तरह दूर रहने की बात काव्यात्मक अतिशयोक्ति है, चिकित्सकीय गारंटी नहीं।
notes_20240423123428.context: The record is dated 2023-06-19 and names “सूर्योदय” as the prompt. It gives traditional wellness advice, but its promise of avoiding all doctors, medicines, and disease should not be treated as medical fact.

literalEnglish: With Sita’s permission, Hanuman ate the fruit.
Remembering the Lord, he was not even slightly afraid of anyone.
notes_20240423123431.childFriendlyEnglish: After receiving Sita’s permission, Hanuman eats fruit in Lanka and remains brave because his thoughts stay with Rama.
notes_20240423123431.simpleHindiExplanation: रामायण के अशोक वाटिका प्रसंग में हनुमान सीता की अनुमति लेकर फल खाते हैं। राम का स्मरण उन्हें निर्भय बनाए रखता है।
notes_20240423123431.context: The preserved record is dated 2023-06-19 and gives “अनुमति” as the prompt. It appears to refer to Hanuman asking Sita before eating fruit in the Ashoka grove.

literalEnglish: Filled with tremendous zeal, he took no rest.
The son of Maruti set out for Lanka, remembering Rama, the abode of joy.
notes_20240423123441.childFriendlyEnglish: Hanuman’s energy and devotion keep him moving toward Lanka without rest as he remembers Rama and carries out his mission.
notes_20240423123441.simpleHindiExplanation: हनुमान अत्यधिक उत्साह से बिना विश्राम किए लंका की ओर बढ़ते हैं। राम-स्मरण उनकी शक्ति, सुख और कर्तव्यनिष्ठा का आधार बताया गया है।
notes_20240423123441.context: The record is dated 2023-06-20 and names “अत्यधिक” as the prompt. “Maruti’s son,” Lanka, and remembrance of Rama place the verse in Hanuman’s Ramayana journey.

literalEnglish: The earth is travelling all around the sun.
One side has daylight while the other side has night.
notes_20240423123445.childFriendlyEnglish: Earth moves through space and turns so that the side facing the Sun has day while the side turned away has night.
notes_20240423123445.simpleHindiExplanation: दोहा पृथ्वी के सूर्य के चारों ओर घूमने और एक ओर दिन तथा दूसरी ओर रात होने की बात कहता है। वैज्ञानिक रूप से दिन-रात मुख्यतः पृथ्वी के अपने अक्ष पर घूर्णन से होते हैं।
notes_20240423123445.context: The preserved record is dated 2023-06-20 and names “भ्रमण” as the prompt. The verse combines Earth’s orbit around the Sun with the day-night contrast; day and night are specifically caused by Earth’s rotation.

literalEnglish: Politics has now become a game of chaupar.
Nowhere is there harmony like that between Bharata and Shri Rama.
notes_20240423123450.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem compares politics to a competitive board game and says that the selfless love of Rama and Bharata is difficult to find there.
notes_20240423123450.simpleHindiExplanation: राजनीति को चौपड़ के दाँव-पेंच जैसा बताया गया है। इसके विपरीत राम और भरत का प्रेम, त्याग और मेल आदर्श संबंध के रूप में रखा गया है।
notes_20240423123450.context: The record is dated 2023-06-21 and names “चौपड़” as the prompt. It uses a traditional board game as a metaphor for political manoeuvring and contrasts it with the Ramayana bond between Rama and Bharata.

literalEnglish: The Pandavas did not bring Krishna with them into the game of chaupar.
Where Narayana is left behind, victory does not come to hand.
notes_20240423123454.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem says the Pandavas entered the dice game without Krishna’s guidance and lost. It teaches that wise and moral guidance should not be left behind.
notes_20240423123454.simpleHindiExplanation: महाभारत के चौपड़ प्रसंग में पांडवों के साथ कृष्ण न होने को हार से जोड़ा गया है। यह भक्तिपूर्ण व्याख्या है कि नारायण का मार्गदर्शन छोड़ने पर विजय नहीं मिलती।
notes_20240423123454.context: The preserved record is dated 2023-06-21 and names “चौपड़” as the prompt. It offers a devotional interpretation of the Mahabharata dice game; it should not be read as a complete account of why the Pandavas lost.

literalEnglish: The Lord of the whole world dwells in a wooden image.
Shri Krishna’s heart beats within it, though the figure has no hands.
notes_20240423123502.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem marvels at a wooden form of Krishna that is worshipped as living and divine even though its carved body has no hands.
notes_20240423123502.simpleHindiExplanation: काष्ठ की देवमूर्ति में जगत के नाथ के निवास का भक्तिपूर्ण भाव है। हाथ-विहीन रूप और कृष्ण के धड़कते हृदय का संकेत संभवतः जगन्नाथ परंपरा से है, पर पंक्ति इसे स्पष्ट नहीं करती।
notes_20240423123502.context: The preserved date is 2023-06-21, while the internal मंच date is 2023-06-22, and the prompt is “काष्ठ.” The wooden, handless Krishna form and living-heart imagery appear to refer to Lord Jagannath and associated devotional tradition, but the identification is inferred.

literalEnglish: At Krishna’s weighing ceremony, Satyabhama was astonished.
As soon as a single tulsi leaf was placed, the offering became complete.
notes_20240423123506.childFriendlyEnglish: The story says Satyabhama’s riches could not balance Krishna, but a tulsi leaf offered with devotion could. Love and sincerity matter more than wealth.
notes_20240423123506.simpleHindiExplanation: कृष्ण के तुलादान की कथा में सत्यभामा बहुत धन रखकर भी तुला नहीं भर पातीं। भक्ति से रखा तुलसी-दल दान को पूर्ण कर देता है, इसलिए भाव धन से बड़ा माना गया है।
notes_20240423123506.context: The record is dated 2023-06-22, its internal date is truncated as 22/6/20, and the prompt is “तुलसी.” It retells the devotional Tulabharam story involving Krishna, Satyabhama, and a tulsi leaf; versions commonly also involve Rukmini.

literalEnglish: In a home where tulsi grows, neither grief nor illness spreads.
Without tulsi, the offering for dark-hued Krishna is incomplete.
notes_20240423123509.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem honours tulsi as a sacred household plant and an important offering to Krishna. Its promise against all sorrow and illness expresses faith rather than a medical guarantee.
notes_20240423123509.simpleHindiExplanation: घर में तुलसी रखने की धार्मिक महिमा और कृष्ण-भोग में तुलसी-दल की आवश्यकता बताई गई है। शोक और रोग न आने की बात श्रद्धा-आधारित काव्यात्मक विश्वास है।
notes_20240423123509.context: The record is dated 2023-06-22, with a truncated internal date of 22/6/20, and names “तुलसी” as the prompt. It combines Vaishnava offering practice with a broad traditional claim about household well-being.

literalEnglish: Hearing poetry composed in metre brings delight.
Poetic faults diminish the aesthetic flavour of a poem.
notes_20240423123513.childFriendlyEnglish: Well-shaped rhythm can make a poem enjoyable to hear, while mistakes in its craft may weaken the feeling it creates.
notes_20240423123513.simpleHindiExplanation: छंदबद्ध कविता सुनने से आनंद मिलता है, जबकि काव्य-दोष उसके रस और प्रभाव को कम कर सकते हैं। यह कविता की शिल्पगत गुणवत्ता पर टिप्पणी है।
notes_20240423123513.context: The preserved date is 2023-06-22, while the internal मंच date is 2023-06-23, and the prompt text appears malformed as “दोष.” The verse discusses classical ideas of metre, poetic fault, and rasa.

literalEnglish: Through online marketing, women are able to work.
They are receiving good prices on the e-Haat.
notes_20240423123516.childFriendlyEnglish: Online marketplaces can help women sell what they make and reach buyers who may pay them a fairer price.
notes_20240423123516.simpleHindiExplanation: ऑनलाइन विपणन और ई-हाट से महिलाओं को काम तथा अपने उत्पादों के अच्छे दाम मिलने की बात कही गई है। यह डिजिटल बाज़ार के अवसरों पर सकारात्मक दृष्टि है।
notes_20240423123516.context: The record is dated 2023-06-23, its internal date is truncated as 23/6/20, and the prompt is “हाट.” “E-Haat” appears to refer to an online marketplace for women entrepreneurs, likely Mahila E-Haat, though the platform is not fully named.

literalEnglish: The women’s ministry has heard their plea.
Through the e-Haat, it has helped women prosper.
notes_20240423123538.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem credits a government ministry’s online market with responding to women’s needs and helping their businesses grow.
notes_20240423123538.simpleHindiExplanation: महिला मंत्रालय द्वारा महिलाओं की जरूरत सुनने और ई-हाट के माध्यम से उन्हें आर्थिक अवसर देने की प्रशंसा की गई है। “आबाद” यहाँ उन्नति या सहारा मिलने के अर्थ में है।
notes_20240423123538.context: The record is dated 2023-06-23, with a truncated internal date of 23/6/20, and names “हाट” as the prompt. The ministry and e-Haat wording appears to point to the Government of India’s Mahila E-Haat initiative, but the formal name is not written.

literalEnglish: Women artisans conduct business digitally.
The e-Haat trade is being run through mobile phones.
notes_20240423123550.childFriendlyEnglish: Women artisans can use a mobile phone to show and sell their work online, making a traditional market available in digital form.
notes_20240423123550.simpleHindiExplanation: महिला कारीगर मोबाइल और ई-हाट के सहारे डिजिटल कारोबार कर रही हैं। दोहा तकनीक से बाज़ार तक पहुँच आसान होने का चित्र देता है।
notes_20240423123550.context: The record is dated 2023-06-23, its internal date is truncated as 23/6/20, and the prompt is “हाट.” It continues the sequence about women artisans using an e-Haat platform; the exact service is inferred rather than fully named.

literalEnglish: Growing angry, Ramachandra aimed his arrow.
When the flame rose in his heart, the ocean’s pride was broken.
notes_20240423123611.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem recalls Rama becoming angry when the ocean did not answer his request. As Rama prepares an arrow, the proud ocean is compelled to respond.
notes_20240423123611.simpleHindiExplanation: रामायण के समुद्र-प्रसंग में राम के क्रोधित होकर बाण साधने का वर्णन है। उनके हृदय की ज्वाला देखकर समुद्र का अभिमान टूटता है और वह मार्ग देने को प्रस्तुत होता है।
notes_20240423123611.context: The preserved record is dated 2023-06-24 and names “कुपित” as the prompt. Rama aiming an arrow and humbling the ocean clearly appear to invoke the Ramayana episode before the crossing to Lanka.

literalEnglish: For strong lungs, blow a conch each day.
The respiratory system grows stronger, and vigor shines on the face.
notes_20240423123615.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem recommends the traditional practice of blowing a conch as a breathing exercise meant to build strength and a lively appearance.
notes_20240423123615.simpleHindiExplanation: दोहा प्रतिदिन शंख बजाने को फेफड़ों और श्वसन-तंत्र की मजबूती से जोड़ता है। मुख पर ओज आने की बात स्वास्थ्य और स्फूर्ति के संकेत के रूप में कही गई है।
notes_20240423123615.context: The preserved record is dated 2023-06-24, carries an internal date of 25/6/2023, and names “शंख” as the prompt. Its health claims reflect the poem’s wording and should not be read as medical guidance.

literalEnglish: (1) Anasuya’s power transformed the situation.
Brahma, Vishnu, and Mahesh are swinging in a cradle.
(2) Saraswati, Lakshmi, and Sati are troubled and astonished.
They gaze at the cradle in wonder, their pride gone.
notes_20240423123619.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem retells the story in which the devoted Anasuya turns the three great gods into infants. Their wives arrive amazed and humbled by the sight of them in a cradle.
notes_20240423123619.simpleHindiExplanation: यह रचना अनुसूया की पतिव्रता-शक्ति वाली पौराणिक कथा कहती है। ब्रह्मा, विष्णु और महेश शिशु बनकर पालने में झूलते हैं, और उनकी पत्नियाँ यह देखकर चकित तथा विनम्र हो जाती हैं।
notes_20240423123619.context: The record is dated 2023-06-25, its internal year is truncated as “25/6/20,” and “पालना” is the prompt. The names Anasuya and the three deities strongly ground the poem in the familiar Hindu narrative, though versions differ in detail.

literalEnglish: People were killed or injured in the railway accident.
Three trains collided; it was a terrible calamity.
notes_20240423123623.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem mourns a devastating rail disaster in which three trains became involved and many people were hurt or lost their lives.
notes_20240423123623.simpleHindiExplanation: दोहा तीन रेलगाड़ियों से जुड़ी भीषण दुर्घटना और उसमें हुए जनहानि व घायलों का दुख व्यक्त करता है। “हताहत” शब्द दोनों प्रकार की क्षति को समेटता है।
notes_20240423123623.context: The record is dated 2023-06-25 and names “हताहत” as the prompt. The three-train wording appears to refer to the 2 June 2023 Odisha rail disaster, but the location and event name are not stated, so the identification remains an editorial inference.

literalEnglish: Seeing his relatives and loved ones, Arjuna became despondent.
When Krishna gave him wisdom, the bonds of attachment opened.
notes_20240423123627.childFriendlyEnglish: Arjuna loses heart when he sees family and friends across the battlefield. Krishna’s teaching helps him understand and move beyond the attachment that has trapped him.
notes_20240423123627.simpleHindiExplanation: कुरुक्षेत्र में अपने ही परिजनों को सामने देखकर अर्जुन निराश हो जाते हैं। कृष्ण का ज्ञान उनके मोह के बंधन खोलता है और उन्हें कर्तव्य समझने की दिशा देता है।
notes_20240423123627.context: The record is dated 2023-06-27 and names “हताश” as the prompt. Arjuna’s despair before Krishna’s teaching clearly invokes the opening setting of the Bhagavad Gita.

literalEnglish: Abhijnanashakuntalam is a great play that was written.
Kalidasa’s renown spread across the world stage.
notes_20240423123630.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem praises Kalidasa’s celebrated play Abhijnanashakuntalam and says that this work carried his reputation around the world.
notes_20240423123630.simpleHindiExplanation: दोहा कालिदास के प्रसिद्ध नाटक “अभिज्ञानशाकुंतलम्” की प्रशंसा करता है। रचना के अनुसार इस नाटक ने कालिदास की कीर्ति को विश्वभर में पहुँचाया।
notes_20240423123630.context: The record is dated 2023-06-27 and explicitly gives “नाटक” as the prompt. The named Sanskrit drama and Kalidasa make the literary reference direct.

literalEnglish: To serve their own interests, the opposition parties became one.
To gain power, a supposedly noble idea occurred to them.
notes_20240423123634.childFriendlyEnglish: With gentle political satire, the poem suggests that rival opposition groups discover unity when joining together may help them win power.
notes_20240423123634.simpleHindiExplanation: दोहा विपक्षी दलों की एकता पर व्यंग्य करता है। कवयित्री के अनुसार यह मेल किसी ऊँचे आदर्श से अधिक अपने हित और सत्ता पाने की इच्छा से प्रेरित दिखाई देता है।
notes_20240423123634.context: The record is dated 2023-06-28 and names “मतलब” as the prompt. The second line is syntactically compressed; “नेक” appears ironic, but no particular alliance or election is named.

literalEnglish: In the freedom struggle, everyone spun thread.
Gandhi turned the spinning wheel and bound the country together.
notes_20240423123637.childFriendlyEnglish: The spinning wheel stands for shared work and self-reliance during India’s freedom movement. The poem credits Gandhi’s example with helping unite the nation.
notes_20240423123637.simpleHindiExplanation: यह दोहा स्वतंत्रता आंदोलन में चरखे और सूत कातने की भूमिका याद करता है। गांधी के चरखे को स्वावलंबन और देश को एक सूत्र में जोड़ने वाले प्रतीक के रूप में प्रस्तुत किया गया है।
notes_20240423123637.context: The record is dated 2023-06-28. Although no formal prompt label is preserved, the title “चरखा” and the references to Gandhi and the freedom struggle make the historical symbolism clear.

literalEnglish: The Ganga descended from heaven; who could withstand her current?
Shiva held her within his matted locks, giving her shelter.
notes_20240423123640.childFriendlyEnglish: When the heavenly Ganga descends with overwhelming force, Shiva receives the river in his matted hair so that her fall will not harm the earth.
notes_20240423123640.simpleHindiExplanation: गंगा के स्वर्ग से उतरने पर उनके प्रचंड वेग को सँभालना कठिन था। दोहा बताता है कि शिव ने उन्हें अपनी जटाओं में धारण कर आश्रय दिया और प्रवाह को नियंत्रित किया।
notes_20240423123640.context: The record is dated 2023-06-28, carries an internal date of 29/6/2023, and names “पनाह” as the prompt. The imagery directly invokes the myth of Shiva receiving the descending Ganga.

literalEnglish: Hari-shayani Ekadashi has arrived, and Chaturmas has begun.
Take wholesome sattvic food and also observe a fast.
notes_20240423123644.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem marks the beginning of Chaturmas at Hari-shayani Ekadashi and encourages simple, sattvic eating together with religious fasting.
notes_20240423123644.simpleHindiExplanation: दोहा हरिशयनी एकादशी से चातुर्मास के आरंभ का उल्लेख करता है। इस अवधि में सात्त्विक, अनुकूल आहार लेने और उपवास रखने की धार्मिक सलाह दी गई है।
notes_20240423123644.context: The record is dated 2023-06-29. No explicit prompt label is present; its festival and dietary references are clear, while fasting practices can vary by family and tradition.

literalEnglish: Seated in the Lord’s lap, he spreads radiance.
Every day, the Pole Star provides knowledge of direction.
notes_20240423123648.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem links the child devotee Dhruva with the steady Pole Star. Placed close to God, he shines in the sky and helps travelers recognize direction.
notes_20240423123648.simpleHindiExplanation: रचना भक्त बालक ध्रुव और ध्रुवतारे को एक साथ स्मरण करती है। प्रभु की गोद में स्थान पाने वाला ध्रुव आकाश में चमकता है और स्थिर तारे के रूप में दिशा बताता है।
notes_20240423123648.context: The record is dated 2023-06-30 and names “गोद” as the prompt. “ध्रुव तारा” supports the devotional identification with Dhruva while also referring to the star’s navigational role.

literalEnglish: The neighboring country Pakistan is in a wretched condition.
On the world stage, it now has no standing.
notes_20240423123652.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem offers a sharply critical view of neighboring Pakistan, describing it as being in difficulty and diminished internationally.
notes_20240423123652.simpleHindiExplanation: दोहा पड़ोसी देश पाकिस्तान की स्थिति पर कठोर राजनीतिक टिप्पणी करता है। इसमें देश के भीतर संकट और विश्व स्तर पर घटती प्रतिष्ठा का दावा है, जो कवयित्री का मूल्यांकन है।
notes_20240423123652.context: The record is dated 2023-06-30 and names “पड़ोसी” as the prompt. “पाक” appears to abbreviate Pakistan. The judgment about its global standing is rhetorical and date-bound, not an independently verified factual assessment.

literalEnglish: Neither storm nor lightning could ever prevail against it.
The banyan remained steadfast, always giving cool shade.
notes_20240423123655.childFriendlyEnglish: Through storms and lightning, the banyan does not yield. Its strength allows it to keep offering others the comfort of shade.
notes_20240423123655.simpleHindiExplanation: आँधी और बिजली भी बरगद को डिगा नहीं पातीं। उसका अडिग खड़ा रहना और लगातार ठंडी छाया देना दृढ़ता के साथ परोपकार का भी चित्र बनाता है।
notes_20240423123655.context: The record timestamp is 2023-07-01, while the embedded date says 1/6/2023; the discrepancy may be a source typo. The title “अडिग” supplies the governing idea.

literalEnglish: One is called steadfast when one’s integrity does not waver.
Such a person lives through joy and sorrow with the same balance.
notes_20240423123658.childFriendlyEnglish: A truly steady person keeps their principles in both good times and hard times, meeting happiness and sadness without losing balance.
notes_20240423123658.simpleHindiExplanation: अडिग व्यक्ति का ईमान परिस्थितियों से नहीं डिगता। वह सुख और दुख दोनों में संतुलित रहकर जीवन जीता है और अपने मूल्यों को बनाए रखता है।
notes_20240423123658.context: The record timestamp is 2023-07-01, while its embedded date says 1/6/2023. The poem defines the titled quality “अडिग” in ethical terms.

literalEnglish: Recognize the illusory world as a mirage.
The faster you chase it, the more troubled you become.
notes_20240423123702.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem compares worldly attractions to water seen in a mirage: chasing them harder does not bring satisfaction and only increases confusion.
notes_20240423123702.simpleHindiExplanation: मायावी संसार की इच्छाओं को मृग-मरीचिका जैसा बताया गया है। उनके पीछे जितना तेज भागेंगे, सच्ची तृप्ति मिलने के बजाय उतनी ही बेचैनी बढ़ सकती है।
notes_20240423123702.context: The record is dated 2023-07-02 and bears the title “मृग.” Its explicit “मृग मरीचिका” metaphor grounds the spiritual warning against chasing illusion.

literalEnglish: An innocent rare animal’s life was lost in vain.
The whole world knows of the blackbuck incident.
notes_20240423123705.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem laments the needless death of a protected blackbuck and assumes that the incident it mentions is widely known.
notes_20240423123705.simpleHindiExplanation: दोहा दुर्लभ और निर्दोष काले हिरण की व्यर्थ हुई मृत्यु पर दुख जताता है। “हादसा” किस विशेष घटना को कहता है, यह मूल अभिलेख में स्पष्ट नहीं है।
notes_20240423123705.context: The record is dated 2023-07-02 and titled “मृग.” It may allude to a prominent blackbuck case, but no person, place, or year is named, so identifying a specific incident would be speculative.

literalEnglish: All the masters are composing verse in the manner of bards.
Those who brought tomatoes along remained fully prepared.
notes_20240423123709.childFriendlyEnglish: This playful poem pictures skilled poets writing like traditional praise-singers while carrying tomatoes as if the unusual prompt requires special readiness.
notes_20240423123709.simpleHindiExplanation: यह हल्की-फुल्की मंचीय रचना धुरंधर कवियों को चारण बनकर छंद लिखते दिखाती है। टमाटर साथ रखने और “चाक-चौबंद” रहने का हास्य-संबंध स्पष्ट नहीं, इसलिए इसे शब्द-खेल की तरह पढ़ना सुरक्षित है।
notes_20240423123709.context: The record is dated 2023-07-02 and explicitly names “टमाटर” as the prompt. The link between tomatoes, bards, and preparedness is not explained in the source and may depend on मंच context or a contemporary joke.

literalEnglish: Waves continually rise in the ocean and become storms.
The Himalaya stands unshaken; behold its grandeur.
notes_20240423123713.childFriendlyEnglish: The moving, stormy sea is contrasted with the still Himalaya. The mountain becomes an image of dignity and firmness amid turmoil.
notes_20240423123713.simpleHindiExplanation: समुद्र की उठती लहरों और तूफानों के सामने हिमालय की अचलता रखी गई है। यह तुलना कठिन परिस्थितियों में दृढ़ और गरिमापूर्ण बने रहने का संदेश देती है।
notes_20240423123713.context: The record is dated 2023-07-02, while its embedded date says 1/7/2023. The title “अडिग” and the ocean–Himalaya contrast make the theme direct.

literalEnglish: Kashi is filled with Vishwanath’s radiance.
Its ghats enchant the heart, and its paan has become famous.
notes_20240423123722.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem celebrates three well-known features of Kashi: devotion to Vishwanath, the beauty of the river ghats, and the city’s famous paan.
notes_20240423123722.simpleHindiExplanation: दोहा काशी की धार्मिक और सांस्कृतिक पहचान का चित्र देता है। विश्वनाथ मंदिर का तेज, मन मोहने वाले घाट और प्रसिद्ध बनारसी पान—तीनों को एक साथ सराहा गया है।
notes_20240423123722.context: The record is dated 2023-07-02, carries an internal date of 1/7/2023, and names “पान” as the prompt. Vishwanath, Kashi’s ghats, and paan are all explicit.

literalEnglish: To gain power, politicians keep searching for opportunities.
They engage in manipulation and switch parties every day.
notes_20240423123725.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem criticizes politicians who treat parties as tools for gaining office, changing sides and using questionable tactics whenever it suits them.
notes_20240423123725.simpleHindiExplanation: सत्ता पाने की लालसा में अवसर खोजने वाले नेताओं पर व्यंग्य किया गया है। बार-बार दल बदलना और धांधली करना सिद्धांतहीन राजनीति के संकेत बताए गए हैं।
notes_20240423123725.context: The record is dated 2023-07-03 and names “धांधली” as the prompt. The first line is compressed, but the second clearly grounds the criticism in manipulation and frequent party-switching; no politician is identified.

literalEnglish: Today is the day of Guru Purnima; honor your mother.
She was the very first to give us knowledge of the world.
notes_20240423123728.childFriendlyEnglish: On Guru Purnima, the poem asks us to recognize a mother as a child’s first teacher because she first introduces the child to life and the world.
notes_20240423123728.simpleHindiExplanation: गुरु पूर्णिमा पर माँ को प्रथम गुरु मानकर सम्मान देने की बात कही गई है। वही बच्चे को सबसे पहले संसार, भाषा और जीवन का ज्ञान देती है।
notes_20240423123728.context: The record is dated 2023-07-03, the date of Guru Purnima that year, and titled “गुरु.” The poem itself explicitly identifies the mother as the first teacher.

literalEnglish: No disciple as great as Ekalavya arose in the world.
To honor his teacher, he gave his thumb as an offering.
notes_20240423123732.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem remembers Ekalavya’s extraordinary devotion to his teacher, shown by giving his thumb when it was demanded as guru-dakshina.
notes_20240423123732.simpleHindiExplanation: दोहा एकलव्य को महान और गुरु-भक्त शिष्य के रूप में याद करता है। गुरु-दक्षिणा में अंगूठा देने की कथा उसके समर्पण को दिखाती है, हालांकि आधुनिक पाठक इस माँग की न्यायसंगतता पर प्रश्न भी उठा सकते हैं।
notes_20240423123732.context: The record is dated 2023-07-03 and titled “गुरु.” Ekalavya’s thumb offering directly invokes the Mahabharata episode; the verse praises devotion without discussing the episode’s ethical controversy.

literalEnglish: Groundwater is being extracted, and all the ponds have dried up.
Throats dry with thirst, and living beings are distressed.
notes_20240423123736.childFriendlyEnglish: As groundwater is overused and ponds disappear, people and animals suffer from thirst. The poem warns that water depletion harms every living being.
notes_20240423123736.simpleHindiExplanation: भूजल के अधिक दोहन और तालाबों के सूखने से जल-संकट पैदा होता है। प्यास से मनुष्य और अन्य जीव बेहाल होते हैं, इसलिए जल-संरक्षण की आवश्यकता सामने आती है।
notes_20240423123736.context: The record is dated 2023-07-04 and names “हलक” as the prompt. Its environmental chain—from groundwater extraction to dry ponds and thirst—is explicit.

literalEnglish: Choose carefully, for a government is to be elected.
Your vote is precious; do not consider it worthless.
notes_20240423123740.childFriendlyEnglish: Voting helps choose a government, so the poem urges every voter to think carefully and value the power of their ballot.
notes_20240423123740.simpleHindiExplanation: सरकार चुनते समय सोच-समझकर मतदान करने की सलाह दी गई है। प्रत्येक मत को बहुमूल्य नागरिक अधिकार और जिम्मेदारी माना गया है।
notes_20240423123740.context: The record is dated 2023-07-04 and titled “मत.” The word carries the sense of a vote here, made explicit by “चुनना है सरकार.” No particular election is named.

literalEnglish: Do not throw away and waste organic refuse.
Put it into a dug pit, where it becomes organic compost.
notes_20240423123745.childFriendlyEnglish: Kitchen and garden waste need not be discarded. Placing it in a compost pit can turn it into useful manure for the soil.
notes_20240423123745.simpleHindiExplanation: जैविक कचरे को बेकार फेंकने के बजाय गड्ढे में डालकर खाद बनाने की सलाह है। इससे कचरा घटता है और मिट्टी के लिए उपयोगी जैविक खाद मिलती है।
notes_20240423123745.context: The record is dated 2023-07-04 and titled “मत.” Here “मत” functions as the prohibition “do not,” while the two lines directly describe basic pit composting.

literalEnglish: Do not be needlessly swayed by a beautiful face.
Choose the person whose thoughts are noble.
notes_20240423123749.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem says that appearance alone should not decide whom we trust or welcome into our lives; a person’s values and ideas matter more.
notes_20240423123749.simpleHindiExplanation: केवल सुंदर चेहरा देखकर प्रभावित न होने की सीख दी गई है। किसी व्यक्ति को अपनाने में उसके ऊँचे विचार, चरित्र और मूल्य अधिक महत्त्वपूर्ण माने गए हैं।
notes_20240423123749.context: The record is dated 2023-07-04 and titled “मत.” The advice contrasts outward beauty with “उच्च विचार”; the exact kind of relationship intended is not specified.

literalEnglish: If you ever meet someone poor and destitute, do not insult them.
Who knows in what guise you may encounter God?
notes_20240423123752.childFriendlyEnglish: Treat every struggling person with dignity. The poem reminds us that the divine may appear in an unexpected form, so contempt for another person can become contempt for God.
notes_20240423123752.simpleHindiExplanation: किसी दीन-दरिद्र व्यक्ति का अपमान न करने की सीख दी गई है। हर मनुष्य में ईश्वर का रूप देखने से करुणा, सम्मान और विनम्रता का व्यवहार जन्म लेता है।
notes_20240423123752.context: The record is dated 2023-07-04 and titled “मत.” Its teaching draws on a broad devotional idea that God may be encountered in an unrecognized human form.

literalEnglish: Taking a fearsome form, Kali carried out the destruction.
Drinking Raktabija’s blood, she delivered the world.
notes_20240423123756.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem recalls Goddess Kali defeating Raktabija. She drinks each drop of his blood so that it cannot create another demon, ending the danger to the world.
notes_20240423123756.simpleHindiExplanation: रचना देवी काली और रक्तबीज के युद्ध की पौराणिक कथा कहती है। रक्त की हर बूँद से नया दैत्य बनने से रोकने के लिए काली उसका रक्त पीती हैं और संसार को संकट से बचाती हैं।
notes_20240423123756.context: The record is dated 2023-07-05 and explicitly gives “विकट” as the prompt. Kali’s fearsome form and Raktabija make the Devi Mahatmya episode identifiable.

literalEnglish: The great warrior Arjuna became trapped in a grave dilemma.
How can I aim arrows at my relatives and loved ones?
notes_20240423123800.childFriendlyEnglish: On the battlefield, Arjuna cannot see his opponents as strangers; they are family and people he loves. His question captures the moral crisis that comes before Krishna’s counsel.
notes_20240423123800.simpleHindiExplanation: युद्धभूमि में अर्जुन इस विकट दुविधा से घिरते हैं कि अपने ही परिजनों और प्रियजनों पर बाण कैसे चलाएँ। यही प्रश्न गीता के उपदेश से पहले उनके नैतिक संकट को व्यक्त करता है।
notes_20240423123800.context: The record is dated 2023-07-05 and names “विकट” as the prompt. Arjuna’s reluctance to shoot at kin directly invokes the Bhagavad Gita’s battlefield setting.

literalEnglish: Provided word: “lalit.”
Rich in the fine arts, these dances are greatly renowned.
Bharatanatyam and Kathakali are known in distant countries.
notes_20240423123803.childFriendlyEnglish: Using the provided word “lalit,” the poem celebrates Indian classical dance as a fine art, naming Bharatanatyam and Kathakali as forms admired far beyond India.
notes_20240423123803.simpleHindiExplanation: “ललित” शब्द से जुड़ी यह रचना भारतीय शास्त्रीय नृत्य की प्रसिद्धि बताती है। भरतनाट्यम और कथकली को ललित कलाओं से समृद्ध तथा दूर देशों तक पहचाने जाने वाले रूप कहा गया है।
notes_20240423123803.context: The record is dated 2023-07-05, carries an internal date of 6/7/2023, and includes the malformed metadata line “प्रदतशब्द:-‘ललित’” in the parsed body. The named dance forms make the subject clear.

literalEnglish: Provided word: “countenance.”
Shyam’s innocent countenance is graced by large eyes.
A flute adorns his lips, and a Vaijayanti garland rests on his chest.
notes_20240423123806.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem paints a loving image of Krishna: wide eyes, a flute at his lips, and the Vaijayanti garland across his chest.
notes_20240423123806.simpleHindiExplanation: यह कृष्ण के मनोहर रूप का भक्तिपूर्ण वर्णन है। उनके भोले मुख, विशाल नेत्र, अधरों पर बंसी और हृदय पर वैजयंती माला का चित्र उभरता है।
notes_20240423123806.context: The record is dated 2023-07-07, carries an internal date of 8/7/2023, and includes its malformed “प्रदतशब्द” metadata as a displayed line. “श्याम,” the flute, and Vaijayanti garland identify Krishna.

literalEnglish: Age is bringing experience as the hair turns white.
Experience shows upon the face, making the appearance dignified.
notes_20240423123809.childFriendlyEnglish: White hair and an experienced face are presented not as losses but as signs of a life that has gained wisdom and dignity.
notes_20240423123809.simpleHindiExplanation: उम्र बढ़ने के साथ सफेद होते बालों को अनुभव की निशानी माना गया है। चेहरे पर झलकता जीवन-अनुभव व्यक्ति के रूप को भव्य और सम्माननीय बनाता है।
notes_20240423123809.context: The record is dated 2023-07-09 and explicitly names “केश” as the prompt. The poem gives aging and white hair a positive interpretation.

literalEnglish: When nutrition is deficient, hair turns white.
Looking at the face then brings sadness to the heart.
notes_20240423123812.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem connects poor nutrition with premature greying and describes the disappointment someone may feel on noticing the change in the mirror.
notes_20240423123812.simpleHindiExplanation: रचना खानपान की कमी को बाल सफेद होने से जोड़ती है और चेहरा देखकर होने वाले खेद को व्यक्त करती है। यह स्वास्थ्य-संबंधी सामान्य कथन है, व्यक्तिगत चिकित्सकीय निष्कर्ष नहीं।
notes_20240423123812.context: The record is dated 2023-07-09 and names “केश” as the prompt. Its causal nutrition claim is stated broadly and should not be treated as a complete medical explanation for greying hair.

literalEnglish: Age is bringing experience as the hair turns white.
Experience shows upon the face, making the appearance dignified.
notes_20240423123818.childFriendlyEnglish: In this separately preserved version, greying hair and the marks of experience are praised as giving an older person a stately presence.
notes_20240423123818.simpleHindiExplanation: इस अलग अभिलेखित रचना में धवल केश और चेहरे पर दिखाई देता अनुभव वृद्धावस्था की गरिमा बनते हैं। उम्र को ज्ञान और सम्मान से जोड़कर देखा गया है।
notes_20240423123818.context: The record is dated 2023-07-09 and names “केश” as the prompt. Its verse text matches another preserved record from the same date, but each source note remains separately represented.

literalEnglish: When vitamin B12 becomes low, hair turns white.
Looking at the face then brings sadness to the heart.
notes_20240423123821.childFriendlyEnglish: The poem names low vitamin B12 as a possible reason for greying hair and describes the sadness a person may feel when noticing it.
notes_20240423123821.simpleHindiExplanation: दोहा विटामिन बी-12 की कमी को बाल सफेद होने से जोड़ता है और इस बदलाव पर होने वाला खेद बताता है। कारण की पुष्टि और उपचार के लिए चिकित्सकीय सलाह आवश्यक होगी।
notes_20240423123821.context: The record is dated 2023-07-09 and names “केश” as the prompt. Vitamin B12 deficiency can be associated with hair changes, but the poem’s simple causal statement is not a diagnosis.

literalEnglish: Bhasmasura moved to place his hand upon Shiva’s head.
The Lord of the world became entangled in his own boon.
Hari fashioned the form of Mohini and brought relief to Shiva.
The demon, enchanted by Hari, placed his hand upon his own forehead.
That demon was reduced to ashes, and the boon took effect.
Hari and Shiva were praised throughout the three worlds.

notes_20240423123824.simpleHindiExplanation: भस्मासुर शिव से मिला वरदान उन्हीं पर आजमाना चाहता है। विष्णु मोहिनी रूप बनाकर उसे मोहित करते हैं; वह अपने सिर पर हाथ रखता है और स्वयं भस्म हो जाता है। इस प्रकार शिव संकट से बचते हैं।

notes_20240423123840.simpleHindiExplanation: हनुमान की तीव्र गति और शक्ति का अतिशयोक्तिपूर्ण चित्र है। उनके चरण पड़ते ही पर्वत धँसता-सा लगता है और वे राम के अमोघ बाण की तरह लक्ष्य की ओर बढ़ते हैं।

literalEnglish: The fruit of patience is sweet; always practice contentment.
